sourceContent.headline: Claude vs ChatGPT vs Gemini: Lead Slips to 58%
sourceContent.description: Claude vs ChatGPT vs Gemini: ChatGPT is still primary for 58% of US users while Gemini takes 25%. See who wins each task before you pick a tool.
paragraphs: In the Claude vs ChatGPT vs Gemini race, ChatGPT is still the primary assistant for 58% of US users, but Gemini has climbed to 25%.

The Claude vs ChatGPT vs Gemini contest is reshaping the consumer AI assistant market, as Google Gemini and Anthropic’s Claude rapidly expand their user bases and narrow ChatGPT’s once-dominant lead. While ChatGPT remains the world’s most widely used AI assistant, recent market data indicates its share of primary AI assistant users has declined as rivals gain traction through tighter ecosystem integration, enterprise adoption, and specialized capabilities.

The changing competitive landscape reflects the maturation of the generative AI industry. Rather than relying on a single chatbot, users are increasingly choosing different AI assistants based on specific tasks such as coding, research, productivity, or integration with existing software. This shift has intensified competition among leading AI companies, including OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Microsoft, and Meta.
A recent survey of U.S. AI assistant users found that ChatGPT remains the primary AI assistant for 58% of users , maintaining a clear lead over competitors.
Anthropic Claude: Smaller overall share but strong adoption among technical users.
Other assistants, including Meta AI and Microsoft’s Copilot, continue expanding their user bases.
Google has rapidly expanded Gemini by integrating it across its ecosystem, including:

This built-in distribution has significantly increased Gemini’s adoption without materially reducing Google’s traditional search traffic. Recent market data also shows Gemini’s web traffic and mobile usage have grown sharply over the past year, and Gemini has already overtaken ChatGPT in Instagram creator conversations . Google is also working on cheaper serving infrastructure, including a new AI chip codenamed “Frozen v2” aimed at running Gemini models far more efficiently .
Anthropic’s Claude has emerged as one of the preferred AI assistants for technical and enterprise users.

Research suggests Claude captures a disproportionately large share of coding-related tasks despite having a smaller overall market share, highlighting its strength in specialized professional workflows. Anthropic has been steadily hardening the product for that audience — it recently began testing a new Projects sidebar for Claude Desktop to make long-running work easier to organise.
Instead of one AI assistant dominating every use case, users are increasingly selecting different models for different tasks.
ChatGPT for general-purpose conversations and creativity.
This growing specialization suggests the AI assistant market is evolving toward a multi-platform ecosystem rather than a winner-takes-all environment.

Although ChatGPT’s relative share has declined as competitors expand, it continues to hold the largest overall user base and remains one of the most recognized AI brands globally. At the same time, Google and Anthropic are leveraging their respective strengths — ecosystem integration and enterprise-focused capabilities — to attract new users and diversify the market.

The increased competition is also accelerating innovation, with leading AI companies introducing more capable reasoning models, multimodal features, AI agents, and deeper integrations into everyday software platforms.

The AI assistant market is entering a new phase where growth is being driven not only by model quality but also by ecosystem reach, enterprise adoption, and specialized use cases. While ChatGPT continues to lead in overall usage, Google’s Gemini is rapidly expanding through its integration across Search, Android, and Workspace, while Anthropic’s Claude has established a strong position among developers and enterprise customers.

Rather than signaling the decline of any single platform, the latest trends point to a more competitive and diversified AI ecosystem. As companies continue investing in reasoning capabilities, AI agents, and productivity tools, users are likely to benefit from faster innovation and greater choice, with different assistants increasingly optimized for different tasks instead of competing solely on overall market share.

There is no single winner. ChatGPT leads on overall usage and general-purpose conversation, Gemini wins on Google ecosystem integration across Search, Android, and Workspace, and Claude is favoured for coding and long-document analysis. The survey cited here measures which assistant people use most, not which model is objectively best.

sourceContent.headline: Polypropylene Market Size to Hit USD 293.54 Billion By 2035
sourceContent.description: The global polypropylene market size is expected to hit aorund USD 293.54 billion by 2035, increasing from USD 193.91 in 2025, growing at a CAGR of 5.40%.
paragraphs: The global polypropylene market was valued at USD 193.91 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 293.54 billion by 2035, growing at a CAGR of 14.35% from 2026 to 2035. Market growth is driven by increasing demand for lightweight, durable, and recyclable materials across the packaging, automotive, healthcare, construction, and consumer goods industries. Advancements in recycling technologies, bio-based polypropylene, and circular economy initiatives are further supporting market expansion. Asia Pacific accounted for 56% of the global market share in 2025, driven by its strong petrochemical infrastructure and expanding manufacturing base, while North America and Europe continue to grow through investments in sustainable polymer production and advanced recycling technologies.

The global polypropylene market size accounted for USD 193.91 billion in 2025 and is predicted to increase from USD 202.25 billion in 2026 to approximately USD 293.54 billion by 2035, expanding at a CAGR of 14.35% from 2026 to 2035. The growth of the polypropylene market can be attributed to its low costs, ease of processing, broad spectrum of applications, increasing demand in various industries and innovative breakthroughs in polypropylene development.
Asia Pacific led the global market with the highest market share of 56% in 2025.
By polymer type, the homopolymer segment was the highest revenue holder in 2025.
By process, the injection molding segment accounted highest revenue share in 2025.
By end-use, the automotive segment has held biggest revenue share in 2025.
By applications, the film and sheet segment accounted for a highest revenue share in 2025.

Growing demand for lightweight, durable, and recyclable materials across the packaging, automotive, healthcare, and consumer goods industries is driving sustained expansion of the polypropylene market worldwide. Polypropylene is a thermoplastic polymer manufactured by polymerizing propylene with a minimum of 90% of functional groups. It has good chemical resistance, mechanical properties, moisture resistance, and good processing properties.

The material is processed into injection-molded, extruded, blow-molded, thermoformed, and fiber products, with a variety of applications. Advances in recycling technologies and high-quality recycled polypropylene manufacturing are facilitated by the increased uptake of the circular economy concept and its practices around the globe. Furthermore, the continued production uptick further validates long-term demand for polypropylene in the packaging, automotive, construction, and consumer product production industries.
When AI Meets Polypropylene: Transforming the Polypropylene Market

The integration of artificial intelligence AI can be applied for recycling polypropylene such as for differentiating various types of propylene for precise sorting, in quality control for examining manufacturing defects, for characterization of polymer by analysing data from analytical techniques, in predictive maintenance and for design optimization of polypropylene products thereby improving their functionality and reducing development costs.

The increasing application of polypropylene across various end-use industries including automotive, packaging, medical, building & construction, and many others drives the demand for the product over the upcoming years. Polypropylene is a light weight material that offers broad range of superior properties such as high tensile strength, low moisture resistance, staining resistance, and resistant to various chemical solvents , acids, & bases because of which it is largely preferred in the aforementioned industries.

Shifting trend towards lighter materials in automotive sector in order to improve the fuel efficiency and curb the pollution rate act as a booming factor for the market growth of polypropylene in the industry. Similarly, it is highly preferred as a packaging solution in food & beverage industry owing to its excellent moisture resistance property that increases the life of the packaged food and prevents it from degradation.

On the other hand, lockdown imposed by different governments to control the spread of COVID-19 pandemic has significantly impacted to the consumption of polypropylene as well as its demand has declined rapid across various end-use industries. Manufacturers are facing difficulties while running production lines because of insufficient supply of raw material and restrictions on logistics along with limitations for the movement of people that further cascade negative impact towards the product demand. Besides this, increasing requirement for specialized polypropylene particularly in the healthcare sector in order to manufacture medical gowns, masks, and other safety equipment expected to propel the demand for the product in the upcoming years.
Due to their hydrocarbon resources and petrochemical production facilities, the Middle East has a unique strategic position as an exporter of polypropylene.

Furthermore, producers in the Middle East take advantage of competitively priced propylene feedstocks, ensuring a constant stream of polypropylene exports to Europe, Africa, and South Asia. Long-term supply contracts and regional port-based logistics hubs will only enhance the region's position as an exporter.

As a significant portion of the European Union's polypropylene imports comes from outside Europe, there are many external suppliers that deliver polypropylene to the automotive, packaging, and consumer goods sectors.
The flow of Trade into the EU is significantly affected by environmental regulations, import tariffs, and energy costs, which further reduce producers' ability to compete against EU-based producers.

Shifting trend towards lighter materials in automotive sector in order to improve the fuel efficiency and curb the pollution rate act as a booming factor for the market growth of polypropylene in the industry. Comparatively, North America has a relatively balanced trade profile for polypropylene exports, which are primarily supported by the country's shale-based feedstock advantage and strong domestic consumption of polypropylene.

Recyclable and Circular Polypropylene Solutions Continue to Become Prominent: One of the fastest growing trends on the market currently is the rise of circular and recyclable polypropylene solutions. There has been an influx of manufacturers investing in both mechanical and chemical recycling technologies and producing high-quality recycled polypropylene that meet performance standards for the packaging, automotive, and consumer goods markets.

Lightweight Material Substitution Will Continue to Shape the Market: Lightweight material substitution will shape the market as a significant trend in the automotive and transportation sectors. Typically found as heavy materials (metal and glass), polypropylene is being used as a replacement for such materials because of its excellent strength to weight ratio, high chemical resistance, and great cost effectiveness.

Polymer Modification and Catalyst Advancements are Driving Additional Market Evolution: Advancements in polymer modification and catalyst technologies continue to drive market evolution. For example, factories have begun developing metallocene-based catalysts and producing improved impact-modified polypropylene grades that are capable of providing greater material flexibility, toughness, and thermal resistance than previously offered polypropylenes.

Industry Growth Overview: The growing demand from the automotive and packaging industries is driving the industrial growth of the market. Moreover, a growth in the healthcare, electronics, and construction sectors is also contributing to this growth.

Sustainability Trends: The sustainability trends focus on enhancing the recycling methods to implement a circular economy model and increasing the shift towards biobased polypropene derived renewable sources to meet the regulatory standards.

Major Investors: Large integrated energy and chemical corporations and major asset management firms are the major investors in the market. SABIC, ExxonMobil Chemical Company, Braskem, and Sinopec are some of the major investors in the market.

Long-Term Industry Outlook: The long-term industry outlook for polypropylene is directed toward sustainability, focusing on bio-based alternatives derived from renewable biomass and ethanol, mainly driven by net-zero goals. Scalable chemical recycling, including pyrolysis and depolymerization, will convert mixed plastic waste into virgin-grade materials, while nanomaterial integration unlocks advanced applications in aerospace and medicine, all strictly regulated by stringent global environmental mandates.

Emerging Business Models: Manufacturers are rapidly moving away from linear production and shifting towards modern manufacturing for Circular-as-a-Service (CaaS), where suppliers lease products and manage closed-loop recovery of materials to ensure packaging and components repurposing. Companies are diversifying raw materials by leveraging propane dehydrogenation technology, while utilizing AI, IoT, and blockchain for supply chain traceability of recycled content, thereby buffering overall volatile fossil fuel prices.

Strategic Recommendations for Stakeholders: Stakeholders can drive sustainable growth by investing in circular infrastructure and localized collection networks to secure raw materials. To ensure seamless operations and avoid market friction, stakeholders should monitor updates for polypropylene materials to avoid distribution restrictions. Furthermore, companies should leverage subsidies in government-sponsored Petrochemical and Plastic Parks and prioritize research and development of light weighting to enhance fuel efficiency and comply with emission targets.

Increasing demand for sustainable and lightweight packaging materials across the food and e-commerce industries is expected to drive the market. Its strong position in flexible and rigid packaging is extended with continuous innovation of barrier films made from materials that can be recycled, and the development of packaging innovations. Furthermore, the rising sustainability regulations, expanding packaged food production, and increasing investments in recyclable plastic packaging are projected to sustain long-term demand across global packaging industries.

Hamper Market Growth Through Feedstock Price Volatility

Persistent volatility in propylene and crude oil prices, which is expected to increase production cost uncertainty across the polypropylene value chain, hinders market growth. The shifting prices of resin, coupled with a lack of flexibility in pricing products downstream, can put profits at risk. Furthermore, expanding environmental regulations and sustainability requirements are likely to limit conventional polypropylene consumption in selected applications.

The rise of complex odor signatures and artificial intelligence is changing the way companies utilize electronic nose systems to detect, classify, and respond. In 2026, robot olfaction progress was summarized in a review article in npj Robotics. This outlines the vast progress of digital noses towards increased sensitivity and improved localization of odor sources. This improvement helps with search and rescue operations and quicker identification of gas leaks. These systems are now based on four major types of sensors. Including metal oxide, electrochemical, optical, and field-effect transistors, each with its characteristic advantages and drawbacks.

The miniaturisation of sensors is also moving at a fast pace. In September 2024, the UNIST team developed an ultra-small electronic nose. It can precisely detect and measure the type and concentration of gas. The small device components will reduce the cost of the device and improve its portability for use in mobile diagnostic solutions. The push to move forward continues with healthcare diagnostics. Requireing ultra compact, low-power sensor array structures that are suitable for clinical and even wearable environments. The food quality monitoring process is more or less comparable. Manufacturers want real-time alerts about contamination, instead of waiting for laboratory testing. Furthermore, the collective efforts are bringing e-nose systems out of the research laboratory and into a wide array of practical applications.

The change at the materials level began to manifest itself in mid-2026. Researchers came up with a plan for a so-called artificial olfactory system. Under the guidance of Hyuk-Jun Kwon, a researcher at Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Technology (DGIST). The team systematically investigated the research trends of design methods for metal-organic framework materials, realization of sensors using MOFs, and AI-based odor pattern recognition using MOFs. This roadmap represents a trend towards e-noses capable of distinguishing many more odors. Than previous generations, which were based on metal oxides alone. They will likely shape the construction of the next generation of diagnostic and environmental monitoring devices through 2035.

This trend continued throughout 2025, as the E-Nose market's global value hit USD 426 million. Volume growth is parallel, as shipping volumes increase while the per-unit sensor costs continue to decrease. As a result of improvements in metal-oxide and MEMS manufacturing. Manufacturing prices remain in retreat, as chipmakers turn to an increasingly smaller sensor array for making semiconductors. Sales prices for clinical grade breath analyzers have yet to become competitive with industrial gas-monitoring units. Even a high-tech e-nose can cost over USD 50,000, a price too steep for smaller enterprises and consumers.

Metal-oxide semiconductor (MOS) sensors continue to be the technology of choice in the majority of food safety and industrial applications. Because of their high sensitivity and low production expense. The field-effect transistor and optical sensor type is showing the greatest growth. Driven in part by the need for smaller, wearable devices needed for diagnostics in health care. Exhaled breath analysis is an emerging, convenient, portable, safe diagnostic technique with high interest at the moment. On the other hand, Asia-Pacific is proving to be the most dynamic area with dense research output from institutions all over South Korea, China, and India region. This is paving the way for a wave of strategic developments to be analyzed in the coming years.

The introduction of artificial intelligence (AI) representation is at the heart of almost every strategic move to be seen during the e-nose development in 2026. The Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Technology researcher Hyuk-Jun Kwon has identified a roadmap. Integrating metal-organic framework with AI based on odor pattern recognition in a paper published in Progress in Materials Science. It's the combination of a novel sensing material and machine learning. This enables modern e-noses to identify larger odor libraries than those older single-sensor designs would have been able to in the past. The technology is expected to be adopted fastest in healthcare. Because diagnostic accuracy is strongly related to the ability of algorithms to interpret the noisy, real-world breath.

The technology of sensing is at the core of these individual breakthroughs. This is being connected to the Internet through IoT to form deployable networks. On the future outlook, the best investment opportunities are still in these projects that are being translated from the laboratory to the point-of-care. Laboratory prototypes of sensors are being developed into devices ready for use in both the clinic and industry. This will continue to influence funding priorities throughout the decade and beyond.

Artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and machine learning are being increasingly adopted in healthcare to enhance diagnostics, streamline treatment algorithms, and aid clinical decision making. De-identified health data is emerging as an important asset for pharmaceutical firms, biotech companies, academia, and innovators in digital health to advance their research and development efforts. Developments in cloud computing and other privacy-preserving technologies have made de-identified health data more accessible for research purposes.

Growing collaboration among healthcare providers, technology companies, and research organizations is expected to create new opportunities for responsible data utilization while strengthening compliance with evolving privacy regulations.

Among end users, healthcare providers generated the largest market revenue in 2025, reflecting their role as major producers and users of clinical information. At the same time, pharmaceutical companies are anticipated to register the fastest growth during the forecast period, supported by increasing investments in real-world evidence, biomarker research, and advanced therapeutic development.

Healthcare organizations are focusing on deploying technology solutions that ensure proper handling of data while complying with changing regulations. The expansion of precision medicine, value-based healthcare, and population health initiatives is also creating new opportunities for organizations capable of delivering reliable, privacy-compliant healthcare datasets that support large-scale research and clinical innovation.

On the other hand, the Asia-Pacific region will become the world's most rapidly growing market until 2035 due to its rapid healthcare digitization, development of electronic health systems, biotech investments, and government initiatives to modernize healthcare data.
Leading Companies Focus on Data Innovation and Strategic Partnerships

Competition within the de-identified health data market continues to intensify as organizations invest in advanced analytics, secure data platforms, interoperability solutions, and AI-enabled healthcare intelligence. Strategic collaborations between healthcare providers, technology companies, and pharmaceutical organizations are further strengthening innovation across the industry.

Organizations are expanding deployment across customer engagement, workflow coordination, and operational planning to improve consistency and business outcomes.

Enterprise AI continues to move from isolated projects into broader business deployment models. Companies are combining machine learning, natural-language processing, computer vision, and decision intelligence capabilities to support internal processes and customer-facing activities. As deployment models mature, enterprise AI market growth is being shaped by cloud adoption, scalable computing infrastructure, and increasing demand for measurable business outcomes. Enterprise AI market trends also indicate stronger interest in balancing operational efficiency with governance and business continuity.

Businesses are increasingly integrating artificial intelligence into decision-making environments to support productivity and operational alignment. This shift continues to strengthen enterprise AI market share across multiple business functions while supporting long-term enterprise AI market forecast expectations.

Cloud environments continue to support broader enterprise AI implementation because organizations require scalable deployment and easier integration across distributed systems. Hybrid and edge deployment models are also receiving attention where operational flexibility and data management remain important. These changing preferences continue influencing enterprise AI market growth and enterprise AI market size across regions and industries.

Organizations are placing greater focus on turning enterprise data into practical business insights. Artificial intelligence market adoption within enterprises is increasingly connected to business intelligence, predictive analysis, and operational coordination. This trend supports stronger adoption across both large organizations and smaller enterprises and contributes to changing enterprise AI market trends.

Enterprise AI usage continues expanding across banking, manufacturing, healthcare, retail, telecommunications, automotive, and utilities. Businesses are adapting AI-enabled environments to align with sector-specific operational requirements. This broad application base supports future enterprise AI market forecast expectations and contributes to stronger enterprise AI market share across industry segments.

According to MarketsandMarkets™, the Application Security market size was valued at USD 12.19 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow from USD 13.6 billion in 2026 to USD 23.45 billion by 2031, exhibiting a CAGR of 11.5% during the forecast period. The fast rise of cloud-native applications, microservices architectures, and API-driven development is driving market growth, resulting in a greatly increased attack surface across current software systems. As enterprises accelerate digital transformation and deploy apps more frequently via CI/CD pipelines, security flaws are usually introduced earlier in the development cycle. This is creating a high need for integrated application security solutions that automate vulnerability detection, secure coding techniques, and continuous testing across the software development life cycle (SDLC) to avoid exploitation before deployment.
Download PDF Brochure@ https://www.marketsandmarkets.com/pdfdownloadNew.asp?id=110170194

Rising adoption of DevSecOps and agile software development practices is a key driving factor for the application security market. As organizations accelerate application delivery, integrating security early in the development lifecycle has become essential to prevent costly breaches and compliance issues. Continuous integration and deployment pipelines require automated security testing, vulnerability scanning, and code analysis to ensure secure releases. This shift toward “security as code” is boosting demand for comprehensive application security solutions that can seamlessly support rapid development cycles while maintaining robust protection.
By security testing tools, IAST to register the highest CAGR during the forecast period.

Interactive Application Security Testing (IAST) equips developers with comprehensive contextual data, encompassing vulnerable code locations, potential exploit pathways, and remediation strategies, while significantly mitigating false positive occurrences. Its integration with automated testing frameworks facilitates continuous security validation without necessitating separate security scans. IAST demonstrates particular efficacy for contemporary web applications, application programming interfaces (APIs), microservices, and cloud-native architectures, where insight into runtime behavior is imperative. As organizations strive for expedited vulnerability identification with minimal disruption to software delivery, IAST is experiencing increased adoption as a complementary technology that enhances testing efficiency, accelerates remediation efforts, and fortifies overall application security within agile development environments.
By deployment mode, cloud segment to register highest CAGR during forecast period.

The cloud-based deployment segment is expected to register a higher CAGR than the on-premises segment during the forecast period. The shift toward digital transformation and the growing reliance on cloud ecosystems are driving the rapid adoption of cloud-based application security. With enterprises increasingly deploying SaaS platforms, cloud-native applications, and supporting remote workforce operations, scalable and flexible security solutions have become essential. Cloud-based application security provides benefits such as fast deployment, centralized control, real-time threat detection, and lower infrastructure costs, appealing to organizations of all sizes. Businesses are utilizing these solutions to safeguard web applications, APIs, and microservices while maintaining regulatory compliance. The demand for continuous, automated, and easily updatable security in dynamic IT environments is further fueling the adoption of cloud-based application security platforms across various industry verticals.
By region, North America to hold largest market share during forecast period.

Based on region, North America is estimated to account for the largest share of the application security market during the forecast period, driven by a mature digital infrastructure, high cybersecurity awareness, and early adoption of advanced development practices. Organizations across BFSI, healthcare, government, and enterprise sectors increasingly rely on cloud-native applications, APIs, and mobile platforms, expanding their exposure to software vulnerabilities. Stringent regulatory requirements, such as data protection, operational resilience, and privacy mandates, reinforce the need for continuous and auditable security measures. North America also benefits from the presence of leading application security vendors, including IBM, Checkmarx, Veracode, and Snyk, which accelerate innovation and adoption. sourceContent.description: New research reveals that people with disabilities now account for nearly 7% of US disposable income, with $107 billion in annual discretionary spending, New research reveals that people with disabilities now account for nearly 7% of US disposable income, with $107 billion in annual discretionary spending, highlighting one of the world's largest – and most overlooked – consumer markets.
paragraphs: New research reveals that people with disabilities now account for nearly 7% of US disposable income, with $107 billion in annual discretionary spending, highlighting one of the world’s largest – and most overlooked – consumer markets.

The US disability consumer market has grown to an estimated $675 billion, according to a major new study from Disability:IN and the American Institutes for Research (AIR), highlighting a significant commercial opportunity for businesses that invest in accessibility, inclusive products and disability-focused customer strategies.

The report, The Next Growth Market: Inside the $675 Billion Consumer Opportunity , examines the purchasing power of working-age adults with disabilities (aged 16–64) and argues that businesses across every sector stand to benefit by designing products, services and customer experiences that better meet the needs of disabled consumers.

The findings build on growing evidence that disability inclusion is not only a social imperative but a commercial one. As previously reported, research has estimated the global disability market to be worth US$13 trillion in annual spending power , making it one of the world’s largest consumer segments. Yet many organisations continue to overlook disabled consumers when designing products, services and customer experiences.

The new research updates AIR’s landmark 2018 report, A Hidden Market: The Purchasing Power of Working-Age Adults with Disabilities , and finds that growing employment among disabled people is helping drive record levels of disposable and discretionary income, creating new opportunities for economic growth and innovation.
The report estimates that the disability consumer market is now worth $675 billion, equivalent in size to the global beauty and cosmetics industry. Researchers found that:
People with disabilities now account for almost 7% of total US disposable income.
Annual discretionary income across the disability community has reached $107 billion.
Approximately 10% of working-age people with disabilities have an average $40,000 in discretionary spending power each year.
Those consumers have an average pre-tax income of $135,805, reflecting a growing segment with significant purchasing power.
According to the report, increasing labour market participation among disabled people is expected to continue strengthening consumer spending over the coming years.

Jill Houghton, President and CEO of Disability:IN, said the findings demonstrate that disability inclusion is increasingly becoming a commercial imperative rather than simply a corporate responsibility initiative. “Our report validates that the once best kept secret in business is no longer,” said Houghton. “The opportunity presented by the $675 billion disability consumer market is enormous, especially for businesses that develop accessible products, emerge as the brand of choice by capturing everyday consumer dollars and include people with disabilities in their go-to-market strategies.”

The study argues that misconceptions around disability and income have often led organisations to overlook one of America’s largest consumer markets. Researchers also note that the report uses the American Community Survey (ACS) definition of disability, covering vision, hearing, mobility, self-care, cognition and independent living.

Importantly, it does not include many people living with chronic illnesses, cancer, neurodivergence, learning disabilities or mental health conditions, meaning the overall disability-related consumer market is likely to be substantially larger than the report measures.

The report highlights growing employment among disabled people as one of the biggest drivers behind rising spending power. Although significant income gaps remain, researchers say improving labour market participation is increasing financial independence and expanding consumer demand. The study found that:
Average disposable income for people with disabilities is approximately $40,000 per year.
Average disposable income for people without disabilities is around $68,000 annually.

As employment opportunities continue to improve, researchers believe the disability economy will continue to expand. The findings also reinforce previous studies showing that employment barriers remain widespread. Research has found that more than half of disabled employees believe their disability makes it harder to progress in their careers , while many continue to fear disclosing invisible disabilities at work because of stigma and discrimination.

New research reveals that people with disabilities now account for nearly 7% of US disposable income, with $107 billion in annual discretionary spending, highlighting one of the world’s largest – and most overlooked – consumer markets.

The US disability consumer market has grown to an estimated $675 billion, according to a major new study from Disability:IN and the American Institutes for Research (AIR), highlighting a significant commercial opportunity for businesses that invest in accessibility, inclusive products and disability-focused customer strategies.

Annual discretionary income across the disability community has reached $107 billion.

Approximately 10% of working-age people with disabilities have an average $40,000 in discretionary spending power each year.

Those consumers have an average pre-tax income of $135,805, reflecting a growing segment with significant purchasing power.

According to the report, increasing labour market participation among disabled people is expected to continue strengthening consumer spending over the coming years.

Jill Houghton, President and CEO of Disability:IN, said the findings demonstrate that disability inclusion is increasingly becoming a commercial imperative rather than simply a corporate responsibility initiative. “Our report validates that the once best kept secret in business is no longer,” said Houghton. “The opportunity presented by the $675 billion disability consumer market is enormous, especially for businesses that develop accessible products, emerge as the brand of choice by capturing everyday consumer dollars and include people with disabilities in their go-to-market strategies.”

The study argues that misconceptions around disability and income have often led organisations to overlook one of America’s largest consumer markets. Researchers also note that the report uses the American Community Survey (ACS) definition of disability, covering vision, hearing, mobility, self-care, cognition and independent living.

Importantly, it does not include many people living with chronic illnesses, cancer, neurodivergence, learning disabilities or mental health conditions, meaning the overall disability-related consumer market is likely to be substantially larger than the report measures.

The report highlights growing employment among disabled people as one of the biggest drivers behind rising spending power. Although significant income gaps remain, researchers say improving labour market participation is increasing financial independence and expanding consumer demand. The study found that:

Average disposable income for people with disabilities is approximately $40,000 per year.

Average disposable income for people without disabilities is around $68,000 annually.

As employment opportunities continue to improve, researchers believe the disability economy will continue to expand. The findings also reinforce previous studies showing that employment barriers remain widespread. Research has found that more than half of disabled employees believe their disability makes it harder to progress in their careers , while many continue to fear disclosing invisible disabilities at work because of stigma and discrimination.

Kathleen Murphy, Managing Researcher at AIR and lead author of the report, said businesses have a clear opportunity to reach an underserved customer base. “People with disabilities represent a powerful segment of the marketplace, with significant opportunity for business performance. In many states, a significant share of this population has discretionary income, giving companies a clear path to expand their reach, capture new demand, and drive sustained growth.”

The report also points to rapid advances in accessible technology as another factor helping strengthen economic participation. Growing adoption of mainstream accessibility features, including assistive AI, screen readers, live captioning, remote accessibility technologies, is making products and services more accessible to a wider range of consumers while enabling greater workforce participation.

Researchers cite wider employment trends, including LinkedIn’s research on disability and employment, suggesting that record numbers of disabled people entering the workforce will continue expanding the disability consumer market across industries and regions.

Martin McKay, Executive Chairman and Founder of Everway, said removing barriers benefits both businesses and society. “One thing is clear: when barriers are removed, neurodivergent individuals and people with disabilities can participate, progress, and contribute at a higher level,” noted McKay. “Inclusion is no longer a side initiative; it’s becoming a strategic priority that reflects how this progress increases economic participation.”

The report outlines several recommendations for organisations seeking to better serve disabled consumers. They include:

Integrate disability into customer research, product development and investment strategies.

Develop wealth-building products and services that reflect the changing income profiles of disabled consumers.

Partner directly with disabled customers to co-create marketing campaigns and brand strategies.

Increase investment through disability-focused funds alongside broader investment portfolios.

Embed accessibility into consumer and enterprise technology to strengthen customer loyalty, win contracts and improve long-term commercial performance.

The recommendations echo wider calls across the disability inclusion movement for organisations to embed accessibility into leadership, strategy and innovation rather than treating it as a compliance exercise.

The report reinforces a consistent message emerging across Fair Play Talks’ disability coverage: organisations that view disability through the lens of opportunity rather than obligation are better positioned to innovate, attract talent and reach new customers.

Business Disability Forum has previously warned that disabled consumers often feel overlooked and disempowered by inaccessible products and services, while research has also highlighted the barriers disabled entrepreneurs continue to face in securing investment and growing businesses. The findings also support recent analysis by Fair Play Talks exploring why leadership commitment remains critical to building genuinely disability-inclusive organisations capable of delivering better outcomes for employees, customers and society .

Closing the report, Houghton said the momentum behind disability inclusion shows no signs of slowing. “If the momentum achieved over the past 10 years is any indication of what the future holds, then we can project with confidence that the favourable trends identified in our research will bear brighter tomorrows for the disability community, businesses at large and the US economy overall.”

sourceContent.headline: Sleep Tech Market Size To Exceed $143.0 Billion By 2035
sourceContent.description: Sleep Tech Market growth is driven by AI-powered monitoring, smart wellness solutions, and rising awareness of sleep health worldwide.
paragraphs: The global Sleep Tech Market is entering a new phase of expansion as consumers, healthcare providers, and employers increasingly recognize quality sleep as a cornerstone of long-term health and productivity. " According to a recent study by SNS Insider, the global Sleep Tech Market size valued at USD 27.46 billion in 2025, is anticipated to grow to USD 143.0 billion by 2035, registering a CAGR of 17.96% over the 2026–2035 forecast period."

As connected health technologies, wearable devices, smart bedding systems, and AI-assisted wellness services become more popular, people are becoming more knowledgeable and aware of their sleep practice. The rise in instances of sleep dysfunction, growing awareness of health issues, and increased digital healthcare infrastructure are paving the way for investment in advanced equipment that is able to offer personalized insight while supporting preventive healthcare strategy for home and hospital environments.
To Get Detailed Insights on the Sleep Tech Market – Request a Sample Report
AI and Digital Health Revolution Reshape Sleep Management

Due to advances in artificial intelligence, the sleep technology industry is rapidly developing. Sleep technology is moving away from basic sleep tracking to provide users with practical advice. In particular, smart ecosystems that include wearable devices, environmental management systems, mobile apps and smart home technology are helping people adjust their sleeping rituals to maximize recovery.

In addition, healthcare professionals are also benefiting from new digital sleep technologies that provide remote monitoring, digital insomnia treatments and artificial intelligence-enhanced diagnostic methods. The corporate world is adding impetus to the growth of the sleep technology industry by encouraging employees to apply these technologies.

Sleep Trackers remained the leading product category, accounting for 35.42% of market revenue in 2025, supported by widespread consumer adoption of smart wearables . Meanwhile, Smart Mattresses are projected to register the fastest growth, advancing at a 19.23% CAGR through 2035 as demand rises for intelligent sleep environments.

Among technologies, Wearable Devices captured 40.33% of global revenue in 2025 due to their convenience and growing health-monitoring capabilities. AI-Enabled Solutions are expected to emerge as the fastest-growing technology segment with a 21.07% CAGR, reflecting increasing demand for predictive analytics and personalized sleep coaching.

By end user, the Residential/Household segment accounted for 48.19% of total market revenue in 2025, while Wellness & Fitness Centers are forecast to expand at the fastest pace with a 20.01% CAGR during the forecast period.

Across distribution channels, Online Retail led the market with a 38.92% revenue share in 2025, whereas Specialty Stores are anticipated to witness the highest growth, progressing at a 20.55% CAGR through 2035.

Technology firms are increasingly integrating sleep solutions into broader digital wellness ecosystems. Customers can now construct customized sleeping environments with little manual intervention thanks to AI-powered coaching platforms, non-contact monitoring sensors, connected lighting systems, automated temperature adjustment, and voice-enabled home assistants. Additionally, innovation in digital therapeutics and remote healthcare is speeding up, making it possible for doctors to monitor patients more efficiently and increase access to evidence-based sleep improvement programs. These improvements are projected to strengthen long-term consumer engagement and create recurring income opportunities across software, subscription services, and linked devices.

With the help of sophisticated healthcare infrastructure, high consumer awareness, and extensive use of digital health technology, North America continued to hold the top spot in 2025. In 2025, the United States generated USD 8.24 billion, accounting for about 85.6% of North American market revenue. The U.S. market is expected to grow at a rate of about 18% CAGR and reach about USD 42.9 billion by 2035.

Through 2035, Asia Pacific is predicted to maintain its position as the fastest-growing regional market because to increased wearable adoption, rising smartphone penetration, and rising investments in digital healthcare. In 2025, China contributed about 41.3% of regional income.

The United Kingdom accounted for 23.7% of regional revenue in Europe, the United Arab Emirates for 28.4% of the Middle East and Africa market, and Brazil for 43.2% of Latin American revenue. These figures demonstrate the increased interest of consumers in linked wellness technology.
Leading Companies Accelerate Innovation Across the Industry

Competition within the global sleep tech industry continues to intensify as companies invest in AI capabilities, biometric sensing, connected hardware, and clinically validated digital health platforms. Strategic product launches, software enhancements, and ecosystem partnerships are strengthening competitive positioning while expanding consumer adoption worldwide.

Major companies operating in the Sleep Tech Market include ResMed Inc., Philips Healthcare (Philips Respironics), Apple Inc., Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd., Garmin Ltd., Fitbit (Google), Oura Health, Eight Sleep Inc., Sleep Number Corporation, Withings SA, Dreem (ResMed), Nox Medical, SleepScore Labs, Beddr Inc., Casper Sleep Inc., Purple Innovation LLC, Tempur-Pedic, Fisher & Paykel Healthcare, Inspire Medical Systems, and SomnoMed .

An SNS Insider analyst Parry Kardani commented, "The convergence of artificial intelligence, connected health ecosystems, and growing awareness of sleep's role in overall wellness is redefining the global sleep technology industry. Companies delivering accurate monitoring, personalized recommendations, and seamless user experiences will be best positioned to capitalize on the market's strong long-term growth trajectory.

July 17, 2026 08:48 ET | Source: BCC Research LLC BCC Research LLC

Boston, July 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The global livestock monitoring market is projected to grow from $6.2 billion in 2025 to $10.3 billion by 2030, representing a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 10.6%, according to a new report from BCC Research titled Global Livestock Monitoring Market . BCC Research is a leading provider of market intelligence and analysis for emerging technologies.

• Robust Market Expansion: The livestock monitoring market will experience strong double-digit growth at 10.6% CAGR through 2030, driven by accelerating digitization of animal agriculture and the increasing need for data-driven herd management across dairy, beef, and poultry operations. • Europe Leads Global Adoption: Europe commands the largest regional market share at 33.2%, reflecting the region's advanced agricultural infrastructure, stringent animal welfare regulations, and early adoption of precision livestock farming technologies. • Precision Farming Revolution: Growing adoption of precision livestock farming (PLF) technologies is transforming traditional farming practices, enabling producers to boost farm productivity, reduce animal mortality, and improve overall herd health while simultaneously lowering operating costs. • Protein Demand Catalyst: Rising global demand for protein is driving productivity optimization initiatives, compelling livestock producers to implement monitoring solutions that maximize output efficiency and ensure consistent supply chains. • Regulatory and Sustainability Focus: Stricter animal welfare regulations and increasing emphasis on sustainable livestock production are creating compliance-driven demand for comprehensive monitoring systems that demonstrate responsible farming practices. • Market Leadership: Key industry players driving innovation include MSD Animal Health, IDEXX Laboratories Inc., Nedap, GEA Group Aktiengesellschaft, DeLaval, Lely, BouMatic, Afimilk Ltd., DAIRYMASTER, and Fancom BV.

The livestock monitoring market's growth trajectory is underpinned by powerful structural forces reshaping modern agriculture. The digitization of animal agriculture represents a fundamental shift toward data-driven farm management, where real-time monitoring capabilities enable producers to make informed decisions about animal health, breeding optimization, and resource allocation. This technological evolution coincides with mounting pressure to increase productivity amid rising global protein consumption, particularly in developing markets where dietary shifts are driving unprecedented demand. Regulatory compliance is emerging as an equally compelling driver, with governments worldwide implementing stricter animal welfare standards and environmental sustainability requirements. These mandates are forcing producers to adopt comprehensive monitoring systems that provide verifiable data on animal treatment, health outcomes, and farming practices, creating sustained demand for advanced surveillance technologies.

The livestock monitoring market presents attractive investment opportunities for technology companies and agricultural equipment manufacturers positioned to capitalize on the sector's digital transformation. Companies developing AI-powered analytics, wearable sensors, and cloud-based management platforms are particularly well-positioned to capture market share. However, investors should consider adoption barriers including high initial capital requirements for smaller farms and connectivity limitations in rural markets. Leading players like IDEXX Laboratories, DeLaval, and GEA Group offer established market positions with proven track records, while emerging technology providers focusing on camera-based analytics and IoT sensor solutions present higher-growth potential despite execution risks.

The report provides comprehensive market sizing, segmentation analysis, competitive intelligence, and five-year forecasts for the global livestock monitoring market. With rising demand for milk and dairy products, increasing urbanization, changing dietary preferences, and government initiatives supporting food security, dairy farmers are moving beyond traditional herd management methods toward intelligent, data-driven operations.

These technologies work together to provide farmers with actionable insights that improve herd efficiency while maintaining high standards of animal welfare.

Efficient herd management allows dairy farms to increase milk yield without significantly increasing herd size, making it an attractive solution for regions seeking greater self-sufficiency.

This impressive growth trajectory is primarily driven by the increasing adoption of automation and digitalization in dairy farming, as producers worldwide strive to enhance productivity, animal health, and overall operational efficiency.

The Dairy Herd Management Market is entering a transformative phase as dairy producers across the Middle East and Africa (MEA) embrace technology-driven farming practices to improve productivity, animal health, and long-term sustainability.

With rising demand for milk and dairy products, increasing urbanization, changing dietary preferences, and government initiatives supporting food security, dairy farmers are moving beyond traditional herd management methods toward intelligent, data-driven operations.

Modern dairy herd management combines advanced monitoring systems, automated feeding technologies, reproductive management tools, health monitoring devices, and cloud-based analytics into a unified ecosystem.

Instead of relying solely on manual observation, farmers now have access to real-time insights that improve decision-making, reduce operational costs, and maximize milk production.

For the Middle East and Africa, where climate challenges, water scarcity, disease outbreaks, and limited skilled labor often affect dairy operations, effective herd management has become more than a productivity tool—it has become an essential strategy for building resilient and profitable dairy businesses.

Dairy herd management refers to the systematic planning, monitoring, and optimization of every aspect of dairy cattle operations. It includes animal nutrition, breeding, reproduction, milk production, disease prevention, health monitoring, genetic improvement, housing conditions, and farm performance analysis.

Today’s dairy herd management systems integrate multiple technologies such as livestock monitoring sensors, RFID identification systems, automated milking equipment, smart feeding systems, farm management software, artificial intelligence analytics, IoT-enabled wearable devices, and cloud-based performance dashboards.

These technologies work together to provide farmers with actionable insights that improve herd efficiency while maintaining high standards of animal welfare.

Food security has become one of the highest priorities for governments across the Middle East and Africa. Heavy dependence on dairy imports has prompted countries to strengthen domestic milk production by investing in modern dairy farming.

Efficient herd management allows dairy farms to increase milk yield without significantly increasing herd size, making it an attractive solution for regions seeking greater self-sufficiency.

Population growth, increasing disposable incomes, and changing consumer lifestyles are driving higher consumption of fresh milk, cheese, yogurt, butter, and other dairy products across the region.

As consumer demand rises, commercial dairy farms are investing in technologies that ensure consistent milk quality, better animal health, and higher production efficiency.

Extreme temperatures, water shortages, and changing environmental conditions present significant challenges for dairy farmers throughout MEA.

Modern herd management technologies help address these issues by: monitoring heat stress, optimizing water consumption, improving feed efficiency, detecting health problems earlier, and reducing production losses

These capabilities are becoming increasingly valuable as climate resilience becomes central to agricultural planning.

Precision Livestock Monitoring. Wearable collars, ear tags, and activity trackers continuously monitor animal movement, feeding behaviour, rumination, body temperature, and reproductive cycles.

Rather than waiting for visible symptoms, farmers receive early alerts that enable preventive care and faster intervention.

Artificial Intelligence in Dairy Farming. Artificial intelligence is changing how dairy farms operate by analyzing large volumes of animal performance data.

AI-powered systems can: predict disease risks, detect estrus more accurately, forecast milk production, recommend feeding adjustments, improve breeding decisions, optimise labour allocation.

These predictive capabilities reduce uncertainty while increasing farm efficiency.

Automated Milking Systems. Automation is gradually gaining momentum in larger commercial dairy operations across the Middle East.

Automated milking systems provide consistent milking schedules, better milk quality, reduced labour requirements, improved animal comfort, and higher operational efficiency.

Although adoption remains limited among smaller farms, larger dairy enterprises increasingly recognize automation as a long-term investment.

Smart Feeding Technologies. Feed represents one of the largest operational expenses in dairy farming.

Smart feeding systems analyze: animal nutritional requirements, milk production levels, feed conversion efficiency, weight gain, and lactation stages.

This enables farmers to reduce feed waste while maximizing milk output.

Countries in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) are investing heavily in advanced dairy infrastructure despite challenging climatic conditions.

paragraphs: Since the arrival of ChatGPT in November 2022, our world has been filled with the term 'generative AI.' Writing text, drawing pictures, and generating code—the AI on our screens has certainly changed the way we work.

However, the person at the center of that frenzy is now beginning to talk about the 'next wave.' That person is Jensen Huang, CEO of semiconductor giant Nvidia. He has been repeatedly mentioning a figure of '$50 trillion,' a scale that is hard to believe.

In this article, I will carefully break down what the next theme Huang calls 'Physical AI' means, analyze the components of that $50 trillion figure, and explain how individual investors should approach this wave, which is being called a 'once-in-a-decade' opportunity. Along the way, I will introduce five noteworthy Japanese stocks that are not yet widely known. I have selected stocks that offer the 'joy of discovery,' rather than household names like Toyota or Sony.

Please note that this article is not intended to recommend the buying or selling of any specific stocks, but is for informational purposes only. Please make investment decisions at your own risk. The author is not an advisor with investment advisory qualifications. Now, let's begin.
To begin with, what is 'Physical AI'?—From inside the screen to the real world

Generative AI may seem omnipotent, but it actually has a major limitation: it cannot leave the screen. Even if it can create text, images, and code, it cannot pick up a cup in front of it, carry luggage, or tighten a screw.

On the other hand, the vast majority of the world's GDP is actually generated in the 'physical world.' Making, transporting, assembling, and repairing things—these labor tasks performed by humans using their bodies are the foundation of the economy. Generative AI has barely touched this massive domain.
That is why evolving AI into an 'intelligence capable of moving in the real world' is attracting attention as the next major frontier. This is the starting point of the concept of 'Physical AI.'
Defining Physical AI—'Perception,' 'Reasoning,' and 'Action'

Simply put, Physical AI is 'AI that perceives, reasons, and acts in the real world.' Nvidia explains the evolution of AI in four major stages. First, 'Perception AI' that recognizes images and sounds; second, 'Generative AI' that creates text and images; third, 'Agentic AI' that autonomously completes tasks; and beyond that is 'Physical AI' that moves in the physical world.

The difficulty of Physical AI lies in the fact that it must 'understand' physical laws such as gravity, friction, and collisions. If a chatbot makes a mistake, it just results in confused text, but if a robot makes a mistake, it could break things or hurt people. That is why developing AI that operates safely in the real world has a completely different level of difficulty compared to generative AI.

This field suddenly became realistic at 'CES 2026,' the world's largest consumer electronics and technology trade show held in Las Vegas in January 2026. At this event, Huang declared that the 'ChatGPT moment' for Physical AI had arrived. It was a declaration that the era in which machines understand, reason, and act in the real world has come. Multiple media outlets have reported on the details of this keynote speech.
https://www.axios.com/2026/01/05/nvidia-ces-2026-jensen-huang-speech-ai

At this CES, Nvidia announced a slew of new technologies, including 'Alpamayo,' an AI for autonomous vehicles; 'GR00T,' a vision-language model for humanoid robots; 'Cosmos,' a foundation model for teaching physical laws to robots; and the next-generation semiconductor platform 'Rubin.' It was also revealed that renowned companies such as Boston Dynamics with its humanoid robot 'Atlas,' Caterpillar with its construction machinery, and Mercedes-Benz with its automobiles are adopting Nvidia's technology. Huang also indicated that robots with some human-like capabilities would appear within 2026.
The following analysis article does a great job of summarizing how CES 2026 was 'all about robots and Physical AI.'

In short, the current situation is that Physical AI, which had been in the research stage, has begun to move into the 'implementation phase' as of 2026. AI that was once confined to screens is now stepping out into factories, warehouses, and roads.

The figure of $50 trillion is so massive that it feels unreal. In Japanese yen, that is well over 7,000 trillion yen. Mr. Huang is not speaking of this figure as the market size for robots alone. He is presenting it as the size of the 'entire industry that physical AI will transform'.

Specifically, this includes the massive industries of manufacturing and logistics, as well as the fields of transportation and mobility. Mr. Huang described this as 'the first $50 trillion industry that the technology sector can reach.' In other words, his argument is that the next decade will be the 'era of autonomous vehicles, robots, and autonomous machines.' You can confirm the details of this statement in the following article.

Specifically, this includes the massive industries of manufacturing and logistics, as well as the fields of transportation and mobility. Mr. Huang described this as 'the first $50 trillion industry that the technology sector can reach.' In other words, his argument is that the next decade will be the 'era of autonomous vehicles, robots, and autonomous machines.' You can confirm the details of this statement in the following article.

What is important is that this $50 trillion is not a 'market available right now.' It is simply the total value of the target industries that physical AI will eventually make more efficient and automate. It is accurate to understand this as the idea that if AI and robots can replace even a few percent of this massive base, a new market worth trillions of dollars will be created.

So, where is the main battlefield for this $50 trillion? We will look at it by dividing it into three major areas.

Main Battlefield 1: Automation of Factories and Logistics

The most realistic area, which is already starting to move, is the automation of factories and logistics. The introduction of robots is already underway in warehouses and production lines where labor shortages are severe. Amazon in the U.S. operates over 750,000 robots in its warehouses, automating the sorting and transport of goods. Walmart is also accelerating the automation of its logistics centers. The following article is a good reference for the expansion of this field.

https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/robotics-physical-ai-here-and-its-coming-50-trillion-market

Factories and warehouses are places where robots can perform best because the environment is organized and tasks are repetitive and predictable. Conversely, many experts believe that a future where humanoid robots walk freely around town is still far off, and for the time being, practical application will center on 'structured environments'.

The second main battlefield is autonomous driving. As Mr. Huang said at CES that 'robotaxis will be the first to benefit,' autonomous vehicles are the most easily understood example of AI moving in the real world.

At the forefront of this is Waymo, a subsidiary of Alphabet (Google's parent company). Waymo currently provides about 500,000 paid rides per week in about 10 U.S. cities, and its fleet of about 3,000 vehicles travels about 4 million miles autonomously per week. It aims to reach 1 million rides per week by the end of 2026, and its corporate value has reached approximately $126 billion.

And what Japanese individual investors cannot overlook is that Waymo plans to enter 'Tokyo,' along with London, as its first overseas expansion destination in 2026. Autonomous driving is becoming a story that is coming to our streets, not something happening far across the ocean. This plan is reported in the following article.

Meanwhile, Tesla is pursuing autonomous driving with its own 'vision-only' approach, and in China, Baidu's Apollo Go and others are commercially deployed in multiple cities. Waymo's 2026 goals and the competitive landscape are summarized in the following article.

The third, and most visionary area, is humanoids, or humanoid robots. Companies around the world, such as Tesla's 'Optimus,' Figure AI's 'Figure,' and China's Unitree and UBTECH, have entered a race for mass production of humanoid robots.

Why 'humanoid'? It is because our society is built on the premise of the 'human body.' Door heights, stair steps, tool shapes, and car driver seats are all designed to fit human dimensions. That is why the logic of those betting on humanoid robots is that if a robot has the same shape as a human, it has the potential to take over all kinds of tasks while using existing social infrastructure.

At CES, Boston Dynamics announced that it would ship its mass-produced Atlas within 2026, and it was reported that South Korea's Hyundai Motor plans to produce 30,000 units annually by 2028. The following article conveys how humanoid robots became the stars of the trade show.

How does physical AI 'move'—three computers and 'AI that learns in virtual space'

sourceContent.headline: 85% of Indian CFOs Face Pressure to Prove AI ROI: Avalara Study
sourceContent.description: Indian finance leaders are accelerating AI adoption, but governance is falling behind. Avalara finds 85% face ROI pressure, while accountability and audit readiness remain gaps.
paragraphs: An Avalara study finds Indian finance leaders are accelerating AI adoption, but governance is lagging, leaving accountability, audit readiness, and compliance gaps unresolved.

Artificial intelligence is moving from experimentation to execution inside finance departments. As AI agents become part of day-to-day financial operations, CFOs are under growing pressure to prove those investments deliver measurable business value. But as enterprises accelerate deployment, governance is struggling to keep pace.

A new global survey by Avalara suggests that Indian finance leaders are moving quickly to deploy AI agents while also facing significant governance challenges. The study points to a widening gap between AI adoption and the controls needed to manage financial risk, regulatory compliance, and accountability.

According to Avalara's report, Agents of Change: How the Race to Deploy AI Agents Is Outrunning Financial Governance, 85% of Indian finance leaders say they face moderate or significant career pressure to prove that AI agent investments are generating returns.
The survey also found that 71% believe the focus inside their organizations is on deploying AI agents quickly, while only 8% say governance takes priority over speed.
The findings suggest AI adoption is increasingly becoming a business mandate rather than just a technology initiative. However, the rush to deploy is exposing new operational risks for finance teams.
The report suggests governance frameworks have yet to catch up with the pace of AI adoption.
27% of Indian respondents said accountability for significant AI agent errors is either unclear or assigned to no one, the highest share among respondents in India, the US, the UK, and Australia.
24% have not updated internal controls in the past year to reflect AI-driven decisions.
Only 28% say AI controls have been reviewed by IT or cybersecurity teams.
10% are not confident they could clearly explain an AI agent's decisions to regulators or auditors, a higher share than respondents in the US, the UK, and Australia.
These findings suggest that while AI is increasingly influencing financial decisions, governance structures are evolving much more slowly.

Commenting on the survey findings, Dulles Krishnan, VP & General Manager, India Operations, Avalara, said: "While Indian enterprises are moving fast to automate, their internal rulebooks are being left behind. Running new AI tools on outdated compliance policies is a massive blind spot. CFOs in this market need to ensure their risk frameworks are actually updated to monitor automated decisions before an auditor comes knocking."

The findings highlight an emerging enterprise challenge. AI adoption is no longer just about automation or productivity. As AI agents begin participating in tax, compliance, and finance operations, organizations also need clear ownership, audit trails, and governance mechanisms.
Without those safeguards, faster deployment could increase regulatory and operational risk instead of reducing it.
The survey also found that 76% of Indian finance leaders lack dedicated in-house expertise to fully understand how their AI agents work.

When asked what would increase confidence in expanding AI deployment, respondents prioritized practical safeguards over additional automation. The most preferred capabilities included AI outputs grounded in verified tax and financial data (27%), human review for higher-risk actions (26%), audit trails documenting every AI action (22%), and stronger vendor commitments around accuracy and accountability (20%).
The responses suggest finance leaders are looking for explainability and oversight as much as efficiency.

sourceContent.headline: AI Infrastructure Spending Holds Near $90 Billion in Q1 2026 as ARM Overtakes x86 in Accelerated Servers; 2026 Forecast Raised to $497 Billion
sourceContent.description: IDC reports Q1 2026 AI infrastructure spending held near $90B as ARM overtook x86 in accelerated servers, with the 2026 forecast raised to $497B.
paragraphs: According to IDC's Worldwide Quarterly AI Infrastructure Tracker, spending reached $89.7 billion in Q1 2026, up 33% year-over-year but flat sequentially as growth normalizes off a larger base. The defining shift was structural: ARM-based rack-scale GPU servers overtook x86 as the dominant accelerated computing platform. IDC raised its full-year 2026 forecast to $497 billion on hyperscaler capex growth and emerging non-GPU AI demand.

The Q1 2026 results confirm that AI infrastructure investment has moved well beyond initial proof-of-concept phases into a sustained, multi-year capital commitment cycle while the competitive battle has shifted from how much compute gets bought to which platform wins it. Enterprise technology buyers, cloud service providers, and national governments are making long term decisions about where to build, how much to spend, and which AI workloads to prioritize.

For vendors, this means a prolonged period of elevated demand across accelerated compute, high-performance storage, and supporting network infrastructure, but also a fast-moving contest for architecture leadership, as ARM rackscale platforms displace x86 in the accelerated server market. For enterprises, the data signals that AI capacity is becoming a structural cost of doing business at scale, that storage refresh deferred during the initial AI buildout can no longer be postponed, and that late movers risk falling behind on both performance and cost efficiency.
IDC now projects the global AI infrastructure market will surpass $1 trillion in 2029, reaching $1.08 trillion, before climbing to $1.21 trillion in 2030.

Regional performance was mixed. The United States remained dominant at $67.9 billion (75.7% of global spend, +30.3% YoY), though growth continues to moderate. China (PRC) returned to growth at $7.8 billion (8.7% share, +9.3% YoY). The Middle East & Africa remained the fastest-growing region (+233% YoY to $1.1 billion), followed by APeJC (+62% to $5.8 billion) and Western Europe (up to $5.1 billion).

Accelerated compute remains the structural backbone, alongside a growing non-GPU AI-centric layer. Server spending represented 97.6% of total AI infrastructure value in Q1 2026, and within that, a growing share of AI-centric demand is landing on infrastructure that isn’t GPU-accelerated at all. AI orchestration tooling, data-pipeline workloads, and CPU-only inference clusters that hyperscalers are running as a cost-mitigation strategy alongside their GPU buildouts.

Deferred storage investment is catching up. After redirecting budget toward GPU and AI server spend for the past one to two years and treating storage refresh as postponable, enterprises can no longer put those purchases off. Pent-up storage refresh is now landing on top of genuine AI-driven demand, reinforcing the urgency behind external storage strategy even as AI-centric storage remains a small share (2.4%) of total AI infrastructure value.

“The Q1 2026 results make clear that AI infrastructure investment has entered a new phase where it’s not just about how much compute gets bought anymore, it’s about which platform wins it. We watched x86 accelerated servers fall from $52 billion to $35 billion in just two quarters while ARM rack-scale platforms nearly doubled, and that’s not demand destruction, that’s an architecture shift that is yet to be definitive as new x86 platforms are on the horizon as well. At the same time, we’re seeing genuine AI-driven demand show up in CPU-only inference clusters, AI orchestration tooling, and a storage refresh with a more AI-related flavor. While global economy and geopolitical tensions seem to slow down other markets, the AI investment pace continues showing an extraordinary resilience to the environment.” — Juan Seminara, Research Director, Worldwide Infrastructure Trackers, IDC
Faster-than-expected scaling of inference workloads as enterprise AI application deployment broadens
Sovereign AI program expansion in the Middle East, Southeast Asia, and Europe, driving incremental greenfield investment
New model architectures and AI agent frameworks require deeper, more distributed compute infrastructure

Emergence of non-GPU AI-centric demand (AI orchestration tooling, data-pipeline workloads, and physical AI use cases such as robotics and autonomous vehicles) extending the addressable market beyond GPU-based training and inference
Power generation and grid capacity constraints, which remain the primary operational bottleneck for new data center commissioning in major markets
Memory and storage component scarcity, which can lift server BOMs and slow procurement cycles, now compounded by enterprises simultaneously catching up on deferred storage refresh
Expanded export controls and data-sovereignty regulations, which could reshape where AI workloads are deployed and which vendors win enterprise deals

Geopolitical instability in the Middle East, where growth is concentrated in a small number of large, government-backed Gulf deals; escalation of regional tensions, including the ongoing conflict involving Iran, could delay procurement decisions, complicate data center siting and security planning, or shift government priorities away from AI infrastructure investment, introducing volatility to what is currently the fastest-growing region

Investors and technology buyers should monitor Q2 2026 capital expenditure guidance from leading hyperscalers and AI platform providers, as these forward signals remain the most reliable leading indicator of near-term infrastructure demand.
