Investors and technology buyers should monitor Q2 2026 capital expenditure guidance from leading hyperscalers and AI platform providers, as these forward signals remain the most reliable leading indicator of near-term infrastructure demand.

Why did AI infrastructure growth moderate from earlier 2025 peaks?

Earlier quarters benefited from a step-change in capital deployment as hyperscalers accelerated training infrastructure buildouts, then a second step-change as ARM rack-scale platforms began displacing x86 in Q4 2025. Q1 2026’s 33% year-over-year growth reflects a much higher base, not a slowdown in demand. Sequential spending was essentially flat with Q4 2025’s record quarter. The long-term expansion cycle remains firmly intact, and IDC’s full-year 2026 forecast was revised upward, not downward, this quarter.

Which regions are emerging as new AI infrastructure centers?

The Middle East, particularly Saudi Arabia and the UAE, again posted the strongest year-over-year growth globally in Q1 2026, driven by government-backed sovereign AI initiatives and partnerships with leading hyperscalers, even as sequential spending pulled back from Q4 2025’s record deal flow. China returned to growth after a Q4 2025 decline. Western Europe and Asia/Pacific also grew sharply, supported by national AI strategies and localized cloud service provider expansion.

Power availability is the single most important operational constraint heading into 2026. Data center commissioning timelines are increasingly driven by utility capacity rather than hardware lead times. In parallel, evolving trade policy, particularly around advanced GPU exports, will continue to reshape competitive dynamics across China, the Middle East, and other emerging markets. The rapid ARM/x86 platform shift also raises execution risk for x86-focused OEMs and ODMs that have not yet diversified their rack-scale roadmaps.

Have ARM servers overtaken x86 in the accelerated server market, and what’s the outlook going forward?

Yes, Non-x86 (ARM) accelerated server value climbed to $53.0 billion in Q1 2026, up from $47.5 billion in Q4 2025 and $29.8 billion in Q3 2025, while x86 accelerated value fell to $34.6 billion from $42.7 billion and $51.9 billion over the same span. The crossover, which began in Q4 2025, reflects large buyers consolidating around NVL72/GB200-class rack-scale platforms and redistributing volume away from custom x86 rack designs. Projections will depend on how offerings evolve. Which platform ultimately prevails remains to be seen, as supply challenges across the industry persist.

For comprehensive vendor share, forecast data, and taxonomy detail, see: IDC Worldwide Quarterly AI Infrastructure Tracker . For taxonomy and methodology definitions, see: Worldwide Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Tracker Taxonomy, 2025 .

Juan Pablo Seminara - Research Director, Worldwide Enterprise Infrastructure Trackers

sourceContent.description: Global spending on AI infrastructure reached $89.7 billion in Q1 2026, representing a 33.1 percent increase year on year, according to IDC
paragraphs: Global spending on AI infrastructure reached $89.7 billion in the first quarter of 2026, representing a 33.1 percent increase year on year, according to IDC’s Worldwide Quarterly AI Infrastructure Tracker.

While spending on AI infrastructure remained flat compared with the previous quarter as growth normalized from a higher base, AI infrastructure market has entered a new phase driven by long-term investment commitments, architecture shifts, and expanding enterprise AI deployments.

IDC has raised its full-year 2026 AI infrastructure spending forecast to $497 billion, reflecting continued hyperscaler capital expenditure, growing enterprise adoption, and rising demand for AI infrastructure beyond GPU-based computing. The global AI infrastructure market will exceed $1.08 trillion in 2029 before reaching $1.21 trillion in 2030, representing a five-year CAGR of approximately 30 percent from 2025.

A major trend in Q1 2026 was the transition from traditional x86 accelerated servers to ARM-based rack-scale GPU platforms, which have become the leading architecture for AI workloads. IDC reported that non-x86 (ARM) accelerated servers generated $53.0 billion in spending during the quarter, compared with $34.6 billion for x86 systems, highlighting a significant shift in AI data center deployments, Juan Seminara, Research Director, Worldwide Infrastructure Trackers, IDC, said in a blog post .

Server infrastructure dominated AI spending, accounting for $87.6 billion, or 97.6 percent of total AI infrastructure investment. Storage spending reached $2.2 billion, representing 2.4 percent of the market. There is growing demand for AI orchestration software, CPU-only inference clusters, and data pipeline infrastructure as hyperscalers seek lower-cost alternatives for selected AI workloads.
United States Maintains Leadership While Middle East Records Fastest Growth

The United States remained the world’s largest AI infrastructure market with $67.9 billion in spending during Q1 2026, representing 75.7 percent of global investment and growing 30.3 percent year over year.
China returned to growth with $7.8 billion, accounting for 8.7 percent of worldwide spending and expanding 9.3 percent compared with a year earlier.

The Middle East and Africa emerged as the fastest-growing region globally, with spending increasing 233 percent year over year to $1.1 billion, supported by sovereign AI initiatives and government-backed investments.

Asia Pacific excluding Japan and China (APeJC) region recorded 62 percent growth to $5.8 billion, while Western Europe reached $5.1 billion as governments and enterprises accelerated AI infrastructure deployment.
AI Infrastructure Spending Continues Multi-Year Expansion
Global AI infrastructure spending reached $318 billion in 2025, more than doubling from $153 billion in 2024, which itself represented 107.6 percent year-over-year growth.

AI infrastructure investment has evolved beyond experimental deployments into a structural, long-term capital investment cycle. Enterprises are also beginning to refresh storage infrastructure after delaying upgrades during the initial wave of GPU investments, creating additional demand across storage systems alongside AI servers.
AI infrastructure spending will expand by approximately 56 percent in 2026, an upward revision from its previous estimate of around 53 percent growth.

Key factors supporting expansion include deployment of enterprise AI inference workloads, increasing sovereign AI programs across the Middle East, Southeast Asia, and Europe, adoption of AI agents and next-generation AI models requiring distributed computing, and growing investment in non-GPU AI infrastructure supporting orchestration platforms, robotics, autonomous vehicles, and AI data pipelines.

However, there are risks that could affect future growth. These include electricity generation and grid capacity limitations delaying new data center construction, shortages of memory and storage components, tighter export controls on advanced AI hardware, evolving data sovereignty regulations, and geopolitical uncertainty affecting AI investments in rapidly growing regions such as the Middle East.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: IDC: Global AI Infrastructure Spending Hits $89.7 Billion in Q1 2026, ARM Servers Overtake x86 as Market Heads Toward $1.21 Trillion by 2030 - InfotechLead

Global spending on AI infrastructure reached $89.7 billion in the first quarter of 2026, representing a 33.1 percent increase year on year, according to IDC’s Worldwide Quarterly AI Infrastructure Tracker.

IDC has raised its full-year 2026 AI infrastructure spending forecast to $497 billion, reflecting continued hyperscaler capital expenditure, growing enterprise adoption, and rising demand for AI infrastructure beyond GPU-based computing.
The global AI infrastructure market will exceed $1.08 trillion in 2029 before reaching $1.21 trillion in 2030, representing a five-year CAGR of approximately 30 percent from 2025.

IDC reported that non-x86 (ARM) accelerated servers generated $53.0 billion in spending during the quarter, compared with $34.6 billion for x86 systems, highlighting a significant shift in AI data center deployments, Juan Seminara, Research Director, Worldwide Infrastructure Trackers, IDC, said in a blog post .
Server infrastructure dominated AI spending, accounting for $87.6 billion, or 97.6 percent of total AI infrastructure investment.
Storage spending reached $2.2 billion, representing 2.4 percent of the market.

United States Maintains Leadership While Middle East Records Fastest Growth The United States remained the world’s largest AI infrastructure market with $67.9 billion in spending during Q1 2026, representing 75.7 percent of global investment and growing 30.3 percent year over year.
China returned to growth with $7.8 billion, accounting for 8.7 percent of worldwide spending and expanding 9.3 percent compared with a year earlier.

The Middle East and Africa emerged as the fastest-growing region globally, with spending increasing 233 percent year over year to $1.1 billion, supported by sovereign AI initiatives and government-backed investments.

Asia Pacific excluding Japan and China (APeJC) region recorded 62 percent growth to $5.8 billion, while Western Europe reached $5.1 billion as governments and enterprises accelerated AI infrastructure deployment.

AI Infrastructure Spending Continues Multi-Year Expansion Global AI infrastructure spending reached $318 billion in 2025, more than doubling from $153 billion in 2024, which itself represented 107.6 percent year-over-year growth.
AI infrastructure spending will expand by approximately 56 percent in 2026, an upward revision from its previous estimate of around 53 percent growth.

paragraphs: Providers who embed oversight and AI management will have an edge.

Worldwide end-user spending on AI models and platforms is projected to total US$64 billion in 2026, up 63.4 per cent from US$39 billion in 2025, with more and more enterprises are choosing to work with companies that can provide clear value.

Spending on generative AI (genAI) models is forecast to grow 117 per cent while AI platform spending will rise 36.9 per cent in 2026, according to Gartner’s latest forecast on AI platforms and models.

“Enterprise AI budgets are coming under greater scrutiny, with increased focus on usage efficiency, cost control and measurable outcomes ,” said the analyst firm’s senior principal research analyst, Arunasree Cheparthi.
“Spending is shifting toward providers who can demonstrate clear value across cost, latency, performance, and reliability.
“This is giving an edge to providers that embed evaluation, cost transparency, and usage tracking into customer workflows, making it easier to manage and optimise AI use.”
However, as spending becomes more usage-driven, providers face pressure to demonstrate real adoption, sustained use, and durable margins.
This dynamic is accelerating growth in domain-specific language models (DSLMs) and specialised models, which are forecast to grow 210 percent in 2026.

According to Gartner, the AI software market is forecast to grow significantly between 2025 and 2026, with total market revenue increasing from US$39.3 billion to US$64.3 billion, representing 63.4 per cent growth.
The Foundation Generative AI Models segment is expected to more than double, rising from US$11.4 billion in 2025 to US$23.4 billion in 2026, representing a growth rate of 104.2 per cent.
Meanwhile, the fastest-growing segment is DSLMs and specialised genAI models, which is projected to expand from US$1.6 billion to US$4.9 billion, achieving 210.0 per cent growth.

AI application development platforms are forecast to grow from US$6.9 billion to US$9.5 billion (up 38.6 per cent), and AI platforms for data science and machine learning are expected to increase from US$19.4 billion to US$26.4 billion (an increase of 36.3 per cent).
Overall, these projections highlight accelerating investment in generative AI technologies, particularly in specialised AI and foundation models .
“Over the long-term, the biggest winners will be vendors that help enterprises manage where and how AI is used across the business ,” said Cheparthi.

“As more models enter the market and usage-based pricing becomes harder to predict, buyers will turn to platforms that help them choose the right tools, monitor performance , enforce policy and keep costs under control.”

Spending on generative AI models is expected to grow 117% in 2026, while AI platforms are forecasted to increase by 36.9%

Worldwide end-user spending on artificial intelligence (AI) platforms and models is projected to reach $64 billion in 2026, up 63.4 per cent from $39 billion in 2025, according to a report by Gartner, a business and technology insights company.
It highlighted that spending on generative AI (GenAI) models is expected to grow 117 per cent in 2026, while spending on AI platforms is forecast to increase 36.9 per cent during the year.

According to Gartner, enterprise AI spending is entering a new phase, with companies paying greater attention to how efficiently AI is being used, how much it costs and whether it delivers measurable business outcomes.

"Enterprise AI budgets are coming under greater scrutiny, with increased focus on usage efficiency, cost control and measurable outcomes," said Arunasree Cheparthi, Senior Principal Research Analyst at Gartner. She said spending is increasingly shifting towards AI providers that can demonstrate value across cost, latency, performance and reliability.

"This is giving an edge to providers that embed evaluation, cost transparency and usage tracking into customer workflows, making it easier to manage and optimise AI use. However, as spending becomes more usage-driven, providers face increasing pressure to demonstrate real adoption, sustained use and durable margins," Cheparthi added.

The report said this trend is driving rapid growth in domain-specific language models (DSLMs) and specialised AI models, which are expected to record the fastest growth among all segments. According to the forecast, spending on Foundation Generative AI Models will increase from $11.4 billion in 2025 to $23.4 billion in 2026, registering a growth of 104.2 per cent.

Worldwide end-user spending on artificial intelligence (AI) platforms and models is projected to reach $64 billion in 2026, up 63.4 per cent from $39 billion in 2025, according to a report by Gartner, a business and technology insights company.

"This is giving an edge to providers that embed evaluation, cost transparency and usage tracking into customer workflows, making it easier to manage and optimise AI use. paragraphs: High margin AI product growth plan builds on Company’s reported 147% YOY revenue growth and $6.6 million net profit from operations in H1 2026.
Genius OS integrates AI Agent teams across Genius School, Genius Academy, Genius Resorts and Genius City models.
Genius OS links to over 300 leading AI models including the latest models from Hermes, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, SpaceX, Meta, Deepseek and Alibaba.
AI product integration follows success of Student AI and Teacher AI, which have scaled to 300,000 users globally in 2026.

SINGAPORE, July 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Genius Group Limited (NYSE American: GNS) ( "Genius Group" , "GNS" or the "Company" ), a leading AI-powered education group, today announced the launch of its full AI-powered product suite, Genius OS. Genius OS is a cohesive family of AI-agent-driven solutions delivering education, acceleration and productivity to students, entrepreneurs and investors across the Company’s four revenue drivers: Genius School, Genius Academy, Genius Resorts and Genius City. Genius Group is rolling out early access to Genius OS initially to its six million students globally, with new users invited to apply for access at www.geniusgroup.ai .

Roger Hamilton, CEO of Genius Group said “We believe the current AI wave is the unique opportunity for a revolution in education to personalized, gamified learning. According to Research and Markets, the AI in education market is forecast to grow 300% from approximately US$10.6 billion in 2026 to US$42.48 billion by 2030 [1] . At this unique moment when AI is moving from single tools to AI agents that act on your behalf, Genius Group has built a full suite of AI agents for every student, entrepreneur and investor we serve .”
The suite spans the Company’s four revenue drivers and is delivered through one operating system and one AI agent layer. Its core products are as follows:

According to Mordor Intelligence, the Japan fresh fruits market size is expected to grow from USD 17.07 billion in 2026 to USD 21.28 billion by 2031, registering a CAGR of 4.55% during the forecast period. The market continues to expand as consumers increasingly seek premium-quality agricultural produce that fits into health-conscious lifestyles. Strong fruit farming heritage, established domestic production systems, and the rising popularity of high-value fruit options continue to support demand across retail and export channels worldwide.

The Japan fresh fruits market growth is also influenced by changing regulatory requirements and evolving corporate expectations regarding structural land management and food supply security. Fruit growers are investing in advanced farming technology adoption while utilizing modern sorting and packaging infrastructures. These developments are helping businesses respond to shifting farm configurations while maintaining high safety protocols and stable supply logistics. Together, these factors continue to strengthen the integrated Japan fresh fruits market forecast across established production zones and expanding urban distribution areas.
Premium Domestic Apple Cultivation Supports Market Value

One of the leading Japan fresh fruits market trends is the sustained consumer preference for top-tier local fruit varieties that command high market prices. Specialized growing regions continue to focus on high-value fruit varieties to meet strict retail benchmarks. The increasing demand for top-grade varieties like Fuji has expanded value generation across both domestic retail sectors and international trading avenues. This steady shift toward high-standard agricultural outputs continues to support the Japan fresh fruits industry.
Import Reliance Gains Stability Across Diverse Product Varieties

While local fruit varieties hold a significant position within the Japan fresh fruits market share, international trade channels for distinct varieties are emerging as an essential segment. The domestic market relies heavily on external supply pathways for items such as bananas, oranges, grapes, and tropical varieties. Global trading operations are expanding their logistics capabilities to satisfy strict regional quality criteria without compromising on structural freshness or product availability.
Government Subsidies and Grants Shape Infrastructure Investment

Another important Japan fresh fruits market trend is the increasing focus on advanced equipment modernization. As farming demographics shift, orchard operators are utilizing government financial support to introduce automation tools and upgraded farming software. These efforts reflect broader agricultural demand for maximized field output while reducing operational hand labor. Specialized technology integration agreements are becoming a vital area of technical development across the Japan fresh fruits industry.
Structural Land Reform Policy Drives Orchard Optimization

Land management practices continue to play a significant role in the Japan fresh fruits market growth. Updated regulatory frameworks regarding agricultural property aim to enhance direct farmer land ownership and minimize historical economic disparities. At the same time, optimized property consolidation is attracting greater interest from commercial farming entities looking to improve scale and expand national food production. These regulatory adjustments help growers balance long-term business security with efficiency targets while meeting national fruit production goals.
Regional Distribution Frameworks and Trade Agreements Create Growth Opportunities

Geographical allocation patterns continue to influence the Japan fresh fruits market forecast. Main production centers, particularly Aomori Prefecture for orchard farming, provide a strong foundation for local supply and premium export lines. Meanwhile, international partnerships with countries like the United States, Chile, Australia, and the Philippines represent active components of the trade architecture, where import entities manage counter-seasonal and tropical supply streams. Evolving logistics networks and strict customs clearance protocols continue to create new opportunities for international suppliers expanding their commercial presence.

sourceContent.description: The global dental services market is projected to grow from USD 523.98 billion in 2026 to USD 795.72 billion by 2035, driven by rising demand for cosmetic and restorative procedures, increasing oral health awareness, and the adoption of digital dentistry technologies.
paragraphs: The global Dental Services Market was valued at USD 499.32 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 795.72 billion by 2035, expanding at a CAGR of 4.77% from 2026 to 2035. Market growth is driven by the rising prevalence of oral diseases, increasing demand for cosmetic and restorative dental procedures, and rapid adoption of digital dentistry technologies such as AI-powered diagnostics, CAD/CAM systems, 3D imaging, and teledentistry. Growing oral health awareness, expanding dental tourism, and investments in advanced dental infrastructure are further supporting global market expansion.
What Is Driving the Growth of the Dental Services Market?

The global dental services market is expanding steadily, driven by rising oral disease prevalence, increasing demand for cosmetic dental procedures, and the adoption of digital dentistry technologies . The market size was valued at USD 499.32 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow from USD 523.98 billion in 2026 to USD 795.72 billion by 2035, registering a CAGR of 4.77% from 2026 to 2035.
North America dominated the market with a major market share of 46% in 2025.
Asia Pacific is expected to grow at the fastest CAGR between 2026 and 2035.
By procedure, the non-cosmetic dentistry segment contributed the highest market share in 2025.
By procedure, the cosmetic dentistry segment is growing at a strong CAGR between 2026 and 2035.
By service, the oral surgery segment held a major market share in 2025.
By service, the orthodontics & prosthodontics segment is expected to expand at a notable CAGR from 2026 to 2035.
By end user, the dental clinics segment generated the biggest market share in 2025.
By end user, the hospitals segment is expanding at the fastest CAGR between 2026 and 2035.

The dental services market involves the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of oral diseases, tooth loss, and structural defects. This market generates revenue from clinics and practitioners and is categorized into three main areas, including preventive care for maintaining oral hygiene, restorative treatments like root canals and dentures for repairing damage, and cosmetic procedures such as implants and teeth whitening to enhance appearance. The growth of this market is driven by the increasing prevalence of oral diseases, advancements in technology, and a heightened consumer focus on aesthetic procedures, which fuel the demand for routine care and improved treatment precision.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing the global market by improving precision in X-ray and 3D image analysis, assisting in treatment planning, and automating administrative tasks. AI algorithms are shifting dentistry from reactive, human-reliant assessments to highly precise, data-driven workflows. For instance, AI can instantly analyze dental radiographs and intraoral scans to detect early signs of cavities, gum disease, and anatomical irregularities, often identifying issues that a human eye might overlook. AI is widely used in orthodontics and implantology to model precise changes before operations commence.

Transformation of Workflows with AI and CAD/CAM : AI-assisted diagnostics help detect early signs of decay and gum disease, allowing for precise orthodontic treatment planning. Technologies like 3D printing and CAD/CAM enable same-day crowns, veneers, and aligners, leading to increased investment in digital workflows that enhance treatment accuracy and patient convenience.

Growing Demand for Cosmetic and Restorative Dentistry : With an increased focus on aesthetics driven by social media and an aging population, cosmetic procedures are in high demand . Invisible orthodontics are becoming popular among adults and teens, replacing traditional metal braces. Lasers are also being used more frequently for pain-free gum sculpting, cavity removal, and accelerated teeth whitening.

Consolidation and the Rise of Dental Service Organizations (DSOs) : The market is experiencing a shift towards corporate consolidation and the establishment of organized dental chains. DSOs handle the business and administrative aspects of dental clinics, allowing dentists to focus on clinical care while scaling operations, standardizing treatment, and expanding access to specialized procedures.

The Shift toward Proactive Oral Health : As awareness of oral hygiene increases, the focus is shifting toward convenience and early, remote intervention. Teledentistry platforms are being utilized for video consultations , reducing the need for in-office visits and allowing for preventative care rather than only reacting to emergencies.

The growing prevalence of dental caries and other oral diseases among the global population is driving the demand for the dental services across the globe. According to the data published by the FDI World Dental Federation, in 2015, around 3.5 billion people were suffering from some kind of oral diseases across the globe. The most common oral health condition was the untreated decay of permanent teeth. The various other factors that drive the market include the rising popularity of dental tourism , increasing demand for the cosmetic dentistry , growing dental implants , and technological advancements in dental services.

The growing awareness regarding oral health among the population, rising disposable income, and rising investments in developing healthcare infrastructure are the key factors responsible for the growth of the dental services market globally. The surging importance of dental support organizations is playing an important role in altering the delivery model of the dental services. The growth of various dental support organizations has significantly fostered the in-house dental services. Dental support organizations are centers that make contracts with the dental service providers and offers management services to provide non-clinical dental services to the consumers. According to the American Dental Association, around 16.3% of the dentists of US were partnered with dental support organizations in 2017. The introduction of invisible teeth braces or aligners have gained rapid traction among the consumers. Moreover, the growing concerns among the young population regarding their aesthetic appearances have encouraged the growth of the global dental services market.

Industry growth Overview: The demand for the dental services industry is being driven by developing digital dentistry solutions such as CAD/CAM systems,3D imaging, lasers, and clear aligners, which creates possibilities for worldwide dental tech companies to reveal localized and advanced solutions.

Global Expansion: Across various cultures, regular practices have continued to encourage oral hygiene routines. In several Middle Eastern and African countries, Miswak sticks have been made from the Salvadora persica tree, which is widely used for its natural antibacterial elements. Such twigs have been utilized for centuries as environment-friendly choices to current toothbrushes, which market oral cleanliness with less environmental impact.

Sustainability Trends: Sustainable practices place importance on utilizing non-toxic and secure materials for fillings, prosthetics, and several other dental implements. This lowers the risk of different feedback and markets complete patient health. Dental practices that concentrate on sustainability are more likely to use environmentally friendly sterilization and cleaning procedures and are less likely to release toxic volatile compounds.

Startup Ecosystem: The startup companies are concentrating on virtual care platforms and tele dentistry. Such digital solutions allow patients to consult with dentists remotely, which enables educational links, and even receive a particular diagnosis from the convenience of their homes. Tele dentistry not only develops access to care, specifically in undeveloped spaces, but also promotes higher flexibility and ease for practitioners and patients alike. Additionally, there is a rising importance on eco-friendliness and sustainability within the dental industry.

The dental services market is primarily driven by the increasing prevalence of oral diseases such as dental caries, periodontal conditions, and tooth loss, which are rising due to changing dietary habits and poor oral hygiene. Growing awareness of oral health and its connection to overall health is also encouraging more people to seek preventive and routine dental care. Additionally, expanding access to dental insurance and improvements in dental technologies such as digital imaging, laser dentistry, and minimally invasive procedures are further supporting market growth.

According to the World Health Organization (WHO), oral diseases pose a major health burden for many countries, affecting people throughout their lifetime and even causing death. It is estimated that oral diseases affect nearly 3.7 billion people.

The Rapid Shift Toward AI-Powered and Digitized Workflows

Digital dentistry and AI are transforming clinical practices by optimizing diagnostics and treatment planning. Technologies such as AI-enabled caries detection, 3D printing, and teledentistry are streamlining workflows, improving accuracy, and reducing appointment times. This technological shift enhances the patient experience, alleviates dental anxiety, and provides holistic, evidence-based care while facilitating high-efficiency operations.

For instance, Overjet is an FDA-cleared dental AI platform adopted by major DSOs to standardize clinical care, increase treatment acceptance, and automate insurance documentation, thus improving diagnostic accuracy and operational efficiency. (Source: https://www.who.int )

Despite its revolutionary potential, the dental services market often faces obstacles due to the high out-of-pocket costs associated with advanced procedures, limiting accessibility. The industry struggles with health insurance reimbursement structures, where global trends heavily rely on out-of-pocket payments for cosmetic and restorative care. Furthermore, workforce shortages and disparities in care access hinder broader commercialization and market penetration.

The market is rapidly moving toward preventive care through tech-enabled teledentistry platforms and subscription-based oral health models. This approach expands market reach to younger and geographically isolated demographics, offering a less intimidating way to access routine checkups. Propelled by rising health awareness and booming dental tourism in certain regions, these virtual and bundled service models are paving the way for long-term, high-margin preventive treatments.

As per our industry expert, the dental services market holds strong growth potential, supported by increasing oral healthcare awareness, rising demand for preventive and cosmetic procedures, and the growing adoption of advanced dental technologies. The expert believes that digital dentistry, AI-driven diagnostics, minimally invasive treatments, and personalized dental care solutions play a crucial role in improving service efficiency and expanding patient engagement. Increasing investments in dental infrastructure, organized dental networks, and technologically advanced clinics are expected to create significant opportunities for market players.

Our industry expert believes that the market is poised for continued expansion as consumers increasingly prioritize oral health as an essential component of overall wellness. The expert highlights that opportunities in dental implants, orthodontics, aesthetic dentistry, and preventive care are expected to accelerate due to demographic changes, rising disposable income, and improved access to dental services. Additionally, emerging markets and innovative care delivery models are likely to provide further avenues for growth by addressing affordability, accessibility, and evolving patient expectations.

LONDON, GREATER LONDON, UNITED KINGDOM, July 27, 2026 / EINPresswire.com / -- "The demand for advanced healthcare technologies is rapidly transforming how neurological conditions are managed. One such innovation gaining significant attention is the artificial intelligence-powered seizure prediction wearable, which offers promising solutions for patients with epilepsy and other neurological disorders. This technology is reshaping patient care by providing timely alerts and improving quality of life.

Market Size and Growth Trajectory of the Artificial Intelligence-Powered Seizure Prediction Wearable Market The market for artificial intelligence-powered seizure prediction wearables has experienced remarkable growth in recent years. It is projected to increase from $1.41 billion in 2025 to $1.73 billion in 2026, reflecting a strong compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 22.5%. This upward trend during the historical period is driven by factors such as the rising prevalence of epilepsy, technological advancements in wearable biosensors, a growing need for early seizure detection, limitations in traditional monitoring methods, and increased neurological research.

Download a free sample of the artificial intelligence-powered seizure prediction wearable market report : https://www.thebusinessresearchcompany.com/sample.aspx?id=28934&type=smp&utm_source=EINPresswire&utm_medium=Paid&utm_campaign=Jul_PR

Future Expansion and Market Forecast for AI-Powered Seizure Prediction Wearables Looking ahead, the market is expected to continue its rapid ascent, reaching $3.87 billion by 2030 with a CAGR of 22.3%. This projected growth is fueled by improvements in AI’s predictive accuracy, the expansion of remote neurology services, increasing demand for real-time seizure alerts, integration of wearables with mobile health applications, and a patient-centered approach to epilepsy management. Emerging trends expected to influence the market include predictive detection of neurological events, continuous EEG monitoring through wearables, personalized seizure alert systems, AI-driven recognition of seizure risk patterns, and enhanced home-based epilepsy care.

What Defines an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Seizure Prediction Wearable? These wearables are devices equipped with advanced sensors combined with AI algorithms that continuously track physiological signals. By analyzing this data in real time, they can predict and alert users about the likelihood of an impending epileptic seizure. Such timely warnings contribute significantly to patient safety and overall quality of life for individuals living with epilepsy.

View the full artificial intelligence-powered seizure prediction wearable market report: https://www.thebusinessresearchcompany.com/report/artificial-intelligence-powered-seizure-prediction-wearable-global-market-report?utm_source=EINPresswire&utm_medium=Paid&utm_campaign=Jul_PR

How Rising Neurological Disorders Propel the Market Forward The increasing incidence of neurological disorders plays a major role in driving the adoption of AI-powered seizure prediction wearables. Neurological diseases, which impair normal brain, spinal cord, or nerve function, are becoming more prevalent largely due to aging populations that are more susceptible to neurodegeneration and related conditions. These wearables assist by persistently monitoring physiological data and using AI to forecast seizures, enabling early interventions that enhance patient safety.

An example illustrating this trend comes from April 2024, when the National Library of Medicine in the US reported that around 6.9 million Americans aged 65 and above are living with Alzheimer’s dementia—a number expected to nearly double to 13.8 million by 2060. Such alarming statistics highlight the growing burden of neurological disorders, which in turn supports expansion in the AI-powered seizure prediction wearable market.

Regional Market Dynamics and Growth Patterns in the AI-Powered Seizure Prediction Wearable Sector In 2025, North America held the largest share of the artificial intelligence-powered seizure prediction wearable market. However, the Asia-Pacific region is anticipated to experience the fastest growth during the forecast period. sourceContent.headline: Biodegradable Plastic Market Size to Hit USD 21.54 Billion by 2035
sourceContent.description: The biodegradable plastics market size was calculated at USD 5.36 billion in 2025 and is projected to hit around USD 21.54 billion by 2035 with a solid CAGR of 14.92%.
paragraphs: The global biodegradable plastic market is projected to grow from USD 5.36 billion in 2025 to USD 21.54 billion by 2035, registering a CAGR of 14.92%. Growth is driven by stringent regulations on single-use plastics, rising environmental awareness, and increasing demand for sustainable packaging solutions. Europe dominates the market due to strong environmental policies, while Asia Pacific is expected to witness the fastest growth, supported by expanding packaging, agriculture, and consumer goods industries, along with AI-driven production optimization and sustainable manufacturing.

The global biodegradable plastics market size was valued at USD 5.36 billion in 2025 and is anticipated to reach around USD 21.54 billion by 2035, growing at a CAGR of 14.92% from 2026 to 2035. The demand for biodegradable plastic market is growing as governments and other agencies across the world are tightening regulations on the usage of non-biodegradable plastics to promote environmentally sustainable options.
Europe led the market with the biggest market share of 42.14% in 2025.
Asia Pacific is estimated to expand at the fastest CAGR during the forecast period.
By Type, the starch-based segment registered the maximum market share in 2025.
By Type, the Polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) segment is expected to expand at the fastest CAGR over the projected period.
By End-use, the packaging segment has held a major revenue share in 2025.
By End-use, the agriculture segment is anticipated to grow at a fastest CAGR between 2026 to 2035.

The biodegradable plastic market refers to the manufacturing and distribution of environmentally friendly plastic or polymer for multiple purposes. Biodegradable plastics are generally made of renewable plant-based materials, such as corn starch, sugarcane, or cellulose, or specialized synthetic polymers. Unlike conventional plastic, they easily break down into natural elements, such as water, carbon dioxide, and biomass. They are predominantly used as packaging materials, agricultural films, and dissolvable stitches, demonstrating their versatility across various industries and their ability to reduce unnecessary plastic waste.
Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Biodegradable plastics

Integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in biodegradable plastic market is going to completely change the industry by optimizing production efficiency and streamlining supply chain management . With AI technology, vast amount of data can be analyzed that helps manufacturers in understanding as well as predicting consumer demands and market trends. This helps the manufacturers o allot resources correctly and in turn, reduce wastage. AI-driven automation technology minimizes chances of human error in production while boosting efficiency of the operations. AI can help improve sustainability metrics for production which will further expand the market. AI technology improves overall efficiency, optimizes supply chain and operations, quality control and reduce waste etc., that benefits the biodegradable plastics industry in the forecast period.

Environmental Sustainability: The increasing focus towards environmental sustainability and stringent government policies necessitates companies to implement sustainable practices in product development, potentiating the demand for biodegradable plastics.

Financial Incentives: Several government and international bodies offer structured financial subsidies and tax breaks to accelerate the production of biodegradable plastics, assisting companies to invest in bioplastic production and research. The “Plastic Park Scheme” was launched by the Indian government to provide a grant funding of up to 50% of the project cost, subject to a ceiling of Rs 40 crore.

Lower Wildlife Risk: The increasing need for saving wildlife creatures also promote the use of biodegradable plastics. Biodegradable plastics are easily decomposed into the soil, eliminating ingestion and entanglement by the wildlife.

Multifunctional Biodegradable Plastics: Scientists develop novel biodegradable plastics with multifunctional properties, such as antimicrobial properties, UV resistance, and improved barrier properties. These multifunctional plastics can be beneficial for a wide range of industries, including healthcare, food, and cosmetics packaging.

Prohibition on the use of single-use plastic along with rising awareness among people related to the ill effects of plastic waste on the environment are the key factors that stimulate the market growth. Non-decomposable plastics stimulate various types of pollution. In order to tackle this problem governments of various regions have banned the use of non-degradable plastics, thereby promoting the application of biodegradable plastics. Moreover, consumers are also willing to pay more for biodegradable plastics due to their eco-friendly nature which boosts the demand for biodegradable plastics in the near future.

Despite numerous advantages, biodegradable plastics have several shortcomings. There is no particular difference between conventional and biodegradable plastics that creates problems while segregating them. Also, the inclusion of conventional plastics in biodegradable plastics landfills causes problems in the decomposition process.

Moreover, not every biodegradable plastic is decomposable in the natural environment. Besides this, they require a specific environment in terms of temperature and moisture for degradation. Further, some of them release harmful gases such as greenhouse gases while decomposition is counterproductive to the environmental cause and restricts their growth in the near future.

The global biodegradable plastics market size was valued at USD 5.36 billion in 2025 and is anticipated to reach around USD 21.54 billion by 2035, growing at a CAGR of 14.92% from 2026 to 2035. The demand for biodegradable plastic market is growing as governments and other agencies across the world are tightening regulations on the usage of non-biodegradable plastics to promote environmentally sustainable options.

Europe led the market with the biggest market share of 42.14% in 2025.

Asia Pacific is estimated to expand at the fastest CAGR during the forecast period.

By Type, the starch-based segment registered the maximum market share in 2025.

By Type, the Polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) segment is expected to expand at the fastest CAGR over the projected period.

By End-use, the packaging segment has held a major revenue share in 2025.

By End-use, the agriculture segment is anticipated to grow at a fastest CAGR between 2026 to 2035.

The biodegradable plastic market refers to the manufacturing and distribution of environmentally friendly plastic or polymer for multiple purposes. Biodegradable plastics are generally made of renewable plant-based materials, such as corn starch, sugarcane, or cellulose, or specialized synthetic polymers. Unlike conventional plastic, they easily break down into natural elements, such as water, carbon dioxide, and biomass. They are predominantly used as packaging materials, agricultural films, and dissolvable stitches, demonstrating their versatility across various industries and their ability to reduce unnecessary plastic waste.

Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Biodegradable plastics

Integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in biodegradable plastic market is going to completely change the industry by optimizing production efficiency and streamlining supply chain management . With AI technology, vast amount of data can be analyzed that helps manufacturers in understanding as well as predicting consumer demands and market trends. This helps the manufacturers o allot resources correctly and in turn, reduce wastage. AI-driven automation technology minimizes chances of human error in production while boosting efficiency of the operations. AI can help improve sustainability metrics for production which will further expand the market. AI technology improves overall efficiency, optimizes supply chain and operations, quality control and reduce waste etc., that benefits the biodegradable plastics industry in the forecast period.

Environmental Sustainability: The increasing focus towards environmental sustainability and stringent government policies necessitates companies to implement sustainable practices in product development, potentiating the demand for biodegradable plastics.

Financial Incentives: Several government and international bodies offer structured financial subsidies and tax breaks to accelerate the production of biodegradable plastics, assisting companies to invest in bioplastic production and research. The “Plastic Park Scheme” was launched by the Indian government to provide a grant funding of up to 50% of the project cost, subject to a ceiling of Rs 40 crore.

Lower Wildlife Risk: The increasing need for saving wildlife creatures also promote the use of biodegradable plastics. Biodegradable plastics are easily decomposed into the soil, eliminating ingestion and entanglement by the wildlife.

Multifunctional Biodegradable Plastics: Scientists develop novel biodegradable plastics with multifunctional properties, such as antimicrobial properties, UV resistance, and improved barrier properties. These multifunctional plastics can be beneficial for a wide range of industries, including healthcare, food, and cosmetics packaging.

Prohibition on the use of single-use plastic along with rising awareness among people related to the ill effects of plastic waste on the environment are the key factors that stimulate the market growth. Non-decomposable plastics stimulate various types of pollution. In order to tackle this problem governments of various regions have banned the use of non-degradable plastics, thereby promoting the application of biodegradable plastics. Moreover, consumers are also willing to pay more for biodegradable plastics due to their eco-friendly nature which boosts the demand for biodegradable plastics in the near future.

Despite numerous advantages, biodegradable plastics have several shortcomings. There is no particular difference between conventional and biodegradable plastics that creates problems while segregating them. Also, the inclusion of conventional plastics in biodegradable plastics landfills causes problems in the decomposition process.

Moreover, not every biodegradable plastic is decomposable in the natural environment. Besides this, they require a specific environment in terms of temperature and moisture for degradation. Further, some of them release harmful gases such as greenhouse gases while decomposition is counterproductive to the environmental cause and restricts their growth in the near future.

The intended breakdown speed of biodegradable polymers is faster than that of conventional plastics. They greatly reduce the long-term waste in landfills and natural ecosystems by breaking down into natural substances like water, carbon dioxide, and biomass through the action of microorganisms. Waste management systems can function more efficiently when biodegradable polymers are used. These products move waste from landfills to composting facilities, where they can be converted into beneficial soil supplements, as they are frequently compatible with composting procedures. When compared to traditional plastics, the manufacture and decomposition of biodegradable polymers typically result in fewer greenhouse gas emissions. This is because they frequently need less energy to make and because the process of their decomposition prevents the production of methane, a strong greenhouse gas that conventional plastics frequently generate as they decompose in anaerobic landfill environments.

The European Union (EU) is taking a remarkable step towards reducing plastic waste by banning single-use plastics by 2030. Single-use plastic packaging items for fresh fruit and vegetables, condiments in fast food restaurants, mini hotel toiletries, and thin plastic bags for groceries make the packaging of everyday items more sustainable. The region is taking several actions on waste management and the circular economy.

For biodegradable polymers to break down efficiently, temperatures above 50°C, which are usually seen in commercial composting facilities, are necessary. The biodegradation process requires a sufficient amount of microbial presence. If the right bacteria are not present in the environment, the degradation process will either proceed much more slowly or not at all. Depending on where they are disposed of, biodegradable plastics might have varying degrees of effectiveness. Inadequate natural decomposition can result in pollution of the environment akin to that produced by traditional plastics. To make sure biodegradable plastics are disposed of properly and may breakdown as intended, waste management systems should be improved and industrial composting facilities should be expanded. maximizing the environmental advantages of biodegradable plastics by educating customers about proper disposal techniques.

Businesses can set themselves apart by funding R&D to produce cutting-edge biodegradable plastic products. These might include materials that perform better overall, like stronger materials or materials that deteriorate more quickly. Businesses can set a higher priority for suppliers who adhere to strict environmental and social responsibility guidelines and put policies in place to cut down on the amount of energy and trash produced during operations. Customers' sense of responsibility can be increased by informing them about the advantages of biodegradable plastics and the significance of safe disposal procedures. Corporate social responsibility can be exhibited by a firm through its philanthropic support of environmental conservation initiatives and active involvement in local communities.

Starch-based plastics are predicted to dominate the global biodegradable plastics market for both revenue and volume and garnered nearly 10.5% of growth rate in terms of revenue during the forecast period. Increasing application of starch-based plastics in end-use industries such as automobiles, packaging, and agriculture attributed to the significant growth of the segment. They are largely helpful in reducing the carbon footprint of conventional resins and encounter significant demand in the agriculture and flexible packaging sectors. Further, starch-based biodegradable plastics are less toxic as they are made up of plant-based materials. The packaging industry is one of the major consumers of starch-based plastics owing to their versatile behavior.

Polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) is anticipated to register the fastest growth over the analysis period. This is attributed to the increasing use of PHA in medical and other applications. PHA is prominently used in medical implants, drug encapsulation, bone marrow scaffolds, tissue engineering, and bone plates. Apart from medical applications, PHA is also used in the packaging of food & beverages, agriculture foil and films, compost bags, and consumer products. The aforementioned factors are expected to fuel the growth of the segment in the coming years.

In 2025, packaging is the leading end-use segment in the global biodegradable plastics market. This is mainly attributed to the shifting consumer trend from synthetic to bio-based products. In food packaging, biodegradable plastics offer promising functionality and are used in numerous applications such as wraps, cups, boxes, and plates. The foregoing trend has gained momentum in the recent past, thus driving the demand for biodegradable plastics. Further, the rising preference for packaged food in accordance with the changing lifestyle positively influences the demand for biodegradable plastics in packaging applications.

On the contrary, agriculture witnessed the fastest growth in the global biodegradable plastics market during the analysis period. This is mainly because of the increasing application of mulch films in agriculture application. Biodegradable mulch film offers greater decomposition compared to other bio-plastics in soil and estimated that nearly 75-80% of the content is renewable thus propelling the market growth of the segment.

The Europe biodegradable plastic market size was estimated at USD 2.27 billion in 2025 and is predicted to be worth around USD 9.47 billion by 2035, at a CAGR of 15.35% from 2026 to 2035.

Europe was a front-runner in terms of revenue in the global biodegradable plastics market in 2025. Rising consumer awareness along with the government of Europe has banned the usage of non-degradable plastics are the key factors that fuel the market growth in the region. Rising soil & environment depletion because of the rising usage of plastics has triggered the need for a shifting trend towards bio-based materials that can be reused and are environment friendly.

The European Commission has set very ambitious circularity objectives for plastics. Regulatory targets of the recently revised waste directives are 10% max landfilling of municipal waste by 2035, 50% recycling of plastic packaging by 2025, and 55% by 2030. Chemical recycling represents a positive step towards reducing the disposed of waste and contributing to a circular economy for plastics. There is also a huge potential for new jobs as the sector develops.

In January 2023, Parliament voted on its position regarding waste shipment rules, which aim to promote reuse and recycling and reduce pollution. MEPs insist that exports of plastic waste to non-OECD countries should be banned and shipments to OECD countries should be phased out within four years.

According to the European Parliament report in March 2025, globally, researchers estimate that the production and incineration of plastic pumped more than 850 million tonnes of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere in 2019. By 2050, those emissions could rise to 2.8 billion tonnes, a part of which could be avoided through better recycling.

The German market is driven by stringent government policies related to circular economy. The German government has launched the “National Circular Economy Strategy (NCES)” to reduce plastic waste and consider all stages of product development from design to recycling. The nation witnessed an investment of €565 million to implement the strategy, of which €260 million will be directed towards the “Future Circular Economy” program.

Since June 1, 2026, GitHub Copilot has charged by the request instead of by the seat, and the change has rippled through every AI coding tool competing for the same developers. Cursor, Anthropic’s Claude Code, and a long tail of smaller agents are now facing the same question GitHub just answered: keep charging a flat monthly fee, or bill for what a developer actually burns through in tokens and compute.

What should Australian developers and businesses budget for?

The stakes go well beyond one vendor’s invoice format. Coding has become the most contested benchmark in AI, and the tools built on top of frontier models are absorbing real inference costs that a $10 or $20 monthly subscription increasingly cannot cover. Mordor Intelligence sizes the global AI code tools market at roughly $9.35 billion in 2026, expanding at more than 26% a year. That growth rate is exactly why flat-rate pricing is breaking down across the industry. This piece breaks down what changed, what it costs now, how Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Code compare, and where AI model pricing goes from here.

Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions.

For years, GitHub Copilot ran on a simple model: pay a flat monthly fee, get effectively unlimited completions, and never think about the meter running. That model ended on June 1, 2026. GitHub moved Copilot onto usage-based billing, charging for premium requests once a plan’s included allowance runs out, at a rate of roughly $0.04 per request under the current schedule. The underlying subscription tiers didn’t disappear. Copilot Pro still lists at $10 a month and Copilot Enterprise at $39 per user per month, but both now sit on top of a metered layer that tracks actual usage rather than assuming it away.

The timing wasn’t random. Agentic coding tools now chew through far more tokens per task than the autocomplete-style Copilot of 2022, because they plan, retry, and self-correct across multiple steps instead of suggesting a single line. GitHub’s own research previously found that Copilot users complete tasks about 55% faster than developers coding without it, a strong pitch for adoption but a rough one for margins once millions of developers start running agentic workflows against the same infrastructure. Usage-based billing is now the norm for GitHub Copilot pricing plans rather than the exception, and rivals are watching closely.

The new math is straightforward once the marketing language gets stripped away. A developer’s monthly Copilot cost now roughly follows this shape:

For a developer who stays inside the included allowance, nothing changes. For a developer running an autonomous agent overnight to refactor a large codebase, the bill can swing hard from one month to the next. That unpredictability, more than the per-request rate itself, is what’s driving the loudest complaints in developer forums, and what finance teams are now being asked to model before signing off on team-wide rollouts.

Every AI coding tool is a thin layer sitting on top of an expensive frontier model, and none of that compute is free. A flat $20 monthly subscription only works if the average user’s token consumption stays well below what that fee actually covers. Agentic tools broke that assumption. Claude Code, Anthropic’s terminal-native coding agent, can run for extended stretches on a single task: reading files, executing commands, and iterating on its own output before returning a finished result. That behaviour is a major reason Claude Code was reported to author close to 4% of all public GitHub commits by early 2026, a figure some analysts expect to pass 20% before the year is out.

Heavier usage per developer means vendors face a choice. Raise flat prices across the board and penalise light users to subsidise heavy ones, or move to metered billing that charges each user closer to their actual draw on the model. GitHub picked the second option. Cursor and Claude Code haven’t gone that far yet, but both already blend a flat subscription with usage limits that kick in once a threshold is crossed, which is really a softer version of the same idea.

Here’s how the three most-searched AI coding tools price their plans as of mid-2026. Every figure below is in US dollars, since all three vendors bill globally in USD, so Australian teams should factor in card-issuer foreign transaction fees on top of the listed price.

None of the three are pure pay-as-you-go yet. All three are hybrids, a flat floor with a usage ceiling, and the direction of travel is the same for all three: less unlimited, more metered. Cursor’s own announcement of its Series D funding round leaned heavily on the growth of paid seats rather than usage volume, which suggests the company is still more comfortable selling subscriptions than metering tokens directly, at least for now.

Sticker price only tells part of the cost story. What actually determines a team’s real monthly bill is how many tokens a tool burns to finish a given task, and that varies a lot between vendors. Industry comparisons circulating in mid-2026 put Claude Code at using roughly 5.5 times fewer tokens than Cursor to complete equivalent coding tasks, a gap credited partly to Claude Code’s higher score on SWE-bench Verified , a widely used benchmark for how well an AI system resolves real-world GitHub issues. Claude Code posts 80.8% on that benchmark according to multiple 2026 comparisons, a figure well ahead of rival scores logged on comparable tasks.

A tool that needs fewer attempts to land a working fix costs less to run even at a higher headline price, because it isn’t burning tokens on retries and dead ends. That’s a genuinely new kind of competitive pressure. Vendors used to compete purely on capability. Now they’re starting to compete on capability per dollar of inference, which rewards accuracy as much as raw power.

Estimates vary sharply depending on which research firm you ask and how broadly they define “AI code tools,” but the more conservative, narrowly scoped estimates cluster in a believable range.

The spread between roughly $9 billion and $34 billion for the same year comes down to scope. Some firms count only dedicated coding assistants such as Copilot and Cursor. Others fold in broader AI-enabled developer platforms and low-code tools with AI features attached. Taking the narrower, more comparable estimates from Mordor Intelligence, Grand View Research, and Research and Markets, the market sits close to $9 to $10 billion in 2026 and is on track for somewhere between $19 billion and $26 billion by 2030. Either way, this is a market growing more than four times faster than typical enterprise software, exactly the kind of growth that makes flat pricing unsustainable for vendors and irresistible for investors at the same time.

Pricing changes at this scale rarely land quietly, and this one hasn’t. Developer forums and team chat channels have carried a steady stream of complaints since June about unpredictable invoices, particularly from teams running agentic workflows overnight without close supervision. The complaint isn’t really about the per-request rate. It’s about not knowing the total until the invoice arrives.

That unpredictability shows up in adoption data too. Surveys circulating in early 2026 put Claude Code’s “most loved” rating among senior engineers at 46%, against 19% for Cursor and 9% for GitHub Copilot, and separate JetBrains-linked data credits Claude Code with a 91% customer satisfaction score and a net promoter score of 54, the highest reported in the category. Adoption splits by company size too. In startups under 50 employees, Claude Code adoption reportedly reaches 75% against 42% for Cursor, while GitHub Copilot holds a commanding 56% share inside companies with more than 10,000 employees, largely on the back of existing Microsoft procurement relationships. Copilot’s installed base remains enormous regardless, with more than 15 million developers across upwards of 77,000 organisations, including a reported 77% of the Fortune 500.

This isn’t the first time software pricing has had to catch up with a cost curve it didn’t anticipate. Cloud computing went through the same transition two decades ago, when fixed-cost hosting gave way to pay-as-you-go compute billed by the second. Enterprise software spent the 2010s moving from perpetual licences to per-seat SaaS subscriptions, another shift driven by vendors needing revenue that tracked usage more closely than a one-time sale ever could.

AI coding tools are simply the latest category to hit the same wall, just much faster. GitHub Copilot launched as a technical preview in 2021 and reached general availability in 2022, running on a flat-fee model from day one. Cursor followed in 2023, built by Anysphere as an AI-native fork of VS Code. Claude Code arrived from Anthropic in 2025, built around agentic, multi-step coding rather than inline completions. All three launched on some version of flat pricing. Four to five years after Copilot’s debut, the entire category is now converging on the metered model that cloud computing adopted decades earlier, only compressed into a fraction of the time.

For a five-person startup, a variable AI tool bill is an inconvenience. For a two-hundred-engineer platform team, it’s a budgeting problem that lands on someone’s desk every quarter. Usage-based pricing means finance teams can no longer multiply headcount by a flat per-seat price and call the forecast done. They now need usage telemetry, spend alerts, and per-team caps, the same FinOps discipline cloud computing teams built up over the past decade, just applied to AI coding spend instead of server bills.

That behaviour is a major reason Claude Code was reported to author close to 4% of all public GitHub commits by early 2026, a figure some analysts expect to pass 20% before the year is out.
The spread between roughly $9 billion and $34 billion for the same year comes down to scope.

Taking the narrower, more comparable estimates from Mordor Intelligence, Grand View Research, and Research and Markets, the market sits close to $9 to $10 billion in 2026 and is on track for somewhere between $19 billion and $26 billion by 2030.

Surveys circulating in early 2026 put Claude Code’s “most loved” rating among senior engineers at 46%, against 19% for Cursor and 9% for GitHub Copilot, and separate JetBrains-linked data credits Claude Code with a 91% customer satisfaction score and a net promoter score of 54, the highest reported in the category.

In startups under 50 employees, Claude Code adoption reportedly reaches 75% against 42% for Cursor, while GitHub Copilot holds a commanding 56% share inside companies with more than 10,000 employees, largely on the back of existing Microsoft procurement relationships.
Copilot’s installed base remains enormous regardless, with more than 15 million developers across upwards of 77,000 organisations, including a reported 77% of the Fortune 500.

records.titleEn: AI Coding Tools Hit $9B as Pricing Goes Metered
records.descEn: GitHub Copilot, Cursor and Claude Code are ditching flat fees for pay-per-token billing in 2026. Here is what's driving the AI pricing shift.
summaryLinesEn: Coding has become the most contested benchmark in AI, and the tools built on top of frontier models are absorbing real inference costs that a $10 or $20 monthly subscription increasingly cannot cover.
GitHub moved Copilot onto usage-based billing, charging for premium requests once a plan’s included allowance runs out, at a rate of roughly $0.04 per request under the current schedule.

Enterprise software spent the 2010s moving from perpetual licences to per-seat SaaS subscriptions, another shift driven by vendors needing revenue that tracked usage more closely than a one-time sale ever could.

sourceContent.headline: Automated Guided Vehicle Market Size to Hit USD 14.04 Bn by 2035
sourceContent.description: The global automated guided vehicle market size is expected to hit around USD 14.04 billion by 2035 from USD 5.77 billion in 2025 with a CAGR of 9.3%.
paragraphs: Automated Guided Vehicle Market (By Type: Unit Load Carriers, Tow Vehicles, Pallet Trucks, Forklift Trucks, Assembly Line Vehicles; By Navigation Technology: Magnetic Guidance, Laser Guidance, Inductive Guidance, Vision Guidance, Natural Navigation, Others; By Application; By Industry; By End User; By Component Type; Hardware, Software, Service; By Battery Type: Lead Battery, Lithium-ion Battery, Nickel-based Battery, Others) - Global Industry Analysis, Size, Trends, Leading Companies, Regional Outlook, and Forecast 2026 to 2035

The global automated guided vehicle market size is calculated at USD 5.77 billion in 2025 and is predicted to increase from USD 6.32 billion in 2026 to approximately USD 14.04 billion by 2035, expanding at a CAGR of 9.3% from 2026 to 2035. This expansion is due to the growing demand for automation across various industries and the rising labor costs.
Europe led the global market with the highest market share of 31% in 2025.
Asia Pacific region is expanding at a CAGR of 11.2% during the forecast period 2026 to 2035.
The natural navigation segment is expanding at a CAGR of 17.5% from 2026 to 2035.
The wholesale and distribution sector is growing at a notable CAGR of 9.3%.
By application, the logistics and warehousing segment accounted for a revenue share of around 41% in 2025.
The assembly segment is expected to drive growth at a CAGR of 13.1% from 2026 to 2035.
By component, the hardware segment dominated the market in 2025 and accounted for a revenue share of over 70%.
The service segment is growing at a CAGR of 9.3% from 2026 to 2035.
By battery type, the lead battery segment has captured a revenue share of around 61% in 2025.
The lithium-ion battery segment is expanding at a CAGR of 15.9%.

The automated guided vehicle market is experiencing strong growth, driven by increasing demand for automation in manufacturing, warehousing, and logistics operations. Companies are adopting the automated guided vehicle approach to improve operational efficiency, reduce labor dependency, and enhance workplace safety. Rapid expansion of e-commerce and omni-channel retail has significantly increased the need for automated advancements in navigation systems, sensors, and fleet management software, which are improving the performance and flexibility.
How does AI contribute to the Expansion of the Automated Guided Vehicle Market?

AI has equipped automated guided vehicles with several features to make them capable of handling strategic and complicated tasks. AI has enhanced the core capabilities of these vehicles by making them more adaptable, smarter, and capable of complicated decision-making. AI has contributed to this enhancement through machine learning for better decision-making, deep learning to adapt to dynamic environments, and computer vision for accuracy and efficiency. Moreover, other forms include natural language processing for facilitating communication, sensor fusion for knowing the surroundings, and reinforcement learning for optimal decision-making.

Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) are self-guided machines designed to autonomously transport materials in industrial environments, including warehouses, factories, and other facilities. Rather than relying on human operators, AGVs utilize a combination of sensors, software, and navigation technology to follow predetermined routes, such as magnetic tape and painted lines. Companies like Mitsubishi Electric have integrated AGVs in their smart factories to enhance productivity and allow workers to focus on higher-value tasks. Warehouses heavily depend on integrating AGVs with Warehouse Management Systems (WMS). The application of AGVs has expanded beyond factories into various industries, including warehousing, automotive, food, medicine, e-commerce, and aerospace.

Factors such as rising production volumes, shorter delivery times, increasing product variety, and persistent skilled labor shortages compel companies to design their internal material flows for greater efficiency and flexibility. AGVs are reliable for managing repetitive and monotonous transport tasks.

The automated guided vehicle market is experiencing growth due to the increasing demand for automation technologies across different industries. This market expansion is driven by improvements in the accuracy, safety, and productivity of AGVs.

It can be integrated into both electric and combustion-engine platforms, and from compact cars to premium models. The system was tested with development vehicles in North America, Europe, and Japan. paragraphs: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), the world’s largest contract chipmaker and a key supplier to Nvidia and Apple, delivered a record-breaking second quarter in 2026 as surging artificial intelligence (AI) demand continued to fuel growth.
TSMC reported 77 percent year-on-year increase in net profit to a record T$706.6 billion (approximately $22 billion), significantly exceeding market expectations.

High Performance Computing (HPC) remained TSMC’s largest business segment, contributing 66 percent of total revenue as demand for AI GPUs, AI accelerators and custom processors from major customers such as Nvidia, AMD, Apple and Broadcom continued to surge.
TSMC’s smartphone business accounted for 22 percent of revenue despite seasonal softness. TSMC’s Internet of Things (IoT) segment contributed 6 percent.
Automotive represented 3 percent of revenue, Digital Consumer Electronics (DCE) generated 1 percent, and other businesses contributed the remaining 2 percent.

Advanced manufacturing technologies continued to dominate wafer revenue. The 2nm process contributed 3 percent, 3nm accounted for 30 percent, and technologies 7nm and below represented 77 percent of total wafer revenue, highlighting the industry’s rapid transition toward leading-edge nodes for AI and high-performance computing workloads.

The latest Omdia report said global smartphone shipments dropped 4 percent in 2Q26 as the memory crisis disrupted supply and pushed up component costs. Apple, one of the main customers of TSMC, has increased its smartphone market share to 20 percent in Q2 2026 from 16 percent in Q2 2025.
Geographically, North America generated 78 percent of TSMC’s revenue in the second quarter, underlining the company’s growing dependence on U.S. hyperscale cloud providers and AI chip designers.

Asia Pacific accounted for 8 percent, China contributed 6 percent, while Japan and Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) each represented 4 percent of total revenue. The regional mix reflects sustained AI infrastructure investments in the United States alongside steady demand from customers across Asia and Europe.

The strong financial performance was driven by sustained demand for advanced semiconductor technologies, including 3nm and 2nm process nodes and advanced CoWoS chip packaging, which are critical for AI accelerators and high-performance computing applications. TSMC also maintained a positive outlook, forecasting more than 40 percent revenue growth for full-year 2026, supported by robust AI infrastructure investments from global technology companies.

Reflecting confidence in long-term AI demand, TSMC increased its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to between $60 billion and $64 billion, up from its earlier upper-end estimate of $56 billion. The higher investment will support capacity expansion for advanced manufacturing technologies and packaging facilities to meet accelerating customer demand.

The company also announced an additional $100 billion investment in Arizona, expanding its total planned U.S. investment to $265 billion. The expansion includes plans for four additional semiconductor fabrication plants, adding to the eight facilities previously announced, strengthening domestic semiconductor manufacturing in the United States while supporting growing AI chip requirements.

TSMC’s market capitalization has climbed to approximately $1.97 trillion, nearly double that of Samsung Electronics, underscoring its dominant position in the global semiconductor industry, Reuters news report said. CEO C.C. Wei said AI demand remains exceptionally strong, with customers continuing to expand investments in advanced computing infrastructure. BABURAJAN KIZHAKEDATH
